translations.text: There was a certain man in the town of Ramathaim-zophim, in the hill country of Ephraim, and his name was Elkanah, son of Jeremiel, son of Elihu, son of Tohu, within the borders of Ephraim.
He had two wives. One was named Hannah and the other Peninnah. Peninnah had children, but Hannah had none.

Following the rites of his worship, the man used to go up from his own city, Ramathaim, to worship God and offer sacrifice in Shiloh. Eli was there, and his two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, the priests of the Lord.
When the time and the day of their offering came, Elkanah made his offering and gave portions to Peninnah.
But to Hannah he gave one portion, because she had no child. Elkanah loved Hannah more than Peninnah, and this was because the Lord had ordered her womb to be closed.
She had no child, and she grieved over this in the thoughts of her heart, because the Lord had ordered her womb to be closed and had not given her a child.
This is how it went year after year when he went up to the temple of the Lord: she would grieve and weep and would not eat bread.
Her husband Elkanah said to her, "Hannah!" She said, "Here I am, lord." Elkanah said to her, "Why do you weep and not eat, and provoke me to anger? Am I not better to you than ten sons?"
After they had eaten in Shiloh, Hannah rose and stood before the Lord. Eli, the priest of the Lord, was sitting on the seat at the threshold of the temple of the Lord.
In the anguish of her heart, Hannah prayed to the Lord with weeping and said:

"O Lord God, if you will look with favour on your handmaid and give me a male heir, I will dedicate him to you, to serve before you under a vow until the day of his death. He shall not even taste wine or strong drink, and no razor shall come upon his head."
As Hannah went on and on with her worship before the Lord, Eli the priest did not leave her alone while she was speaking [?].
She was speaking in her heart. Only her lips were moving, and her voice could not be heard. The Lord heard her, but Eli thought she was drunk.
One of Eli's servants said to her, "How long will you be drunk? Go, withdraw from the presence of the Lord, and put that wine away from you!"
Hannah answered him, "It is not so, lord. I am a woman grieved in heart. I have not even tasted wine or strong drink. I am pouring out my prayers before the Lord."
"Do not think of your handmaid as one of the daughters of the worthless [?]. I have been speaking until now out of the greatness of my griefs."
Eli answered her, "[?] Go in peace, and may the God of Israel grant you everything your heart has asked, whatever you have asked of him."
Hannah said, "Now indeed your handmaid has found favour before you!" Then Hannah went on her way with joy. She ate and drank with her husband, and her face was no longer sad.
They rose early in the morning to worship the Lord, and then set out on their way to Ramathaim. Elkanah went in to his wife Hannah, for the Lord had remembered her.
She conceived and bore a son, and she named him Samuel, for she said, "I asked for him from the Lord God of hosts."
The man Elkanah and all his household went up to offer sacrifice in Shiloh, following the rites of their custom: to fulfil his vows and to offer all the tithes of his land.

But Hannah did not go up with him, for she said to her husband: "I will not go up with you until this child is weaned from the breast. Then I will present him before the Lord, and he shall stay there for all time."
Elkanah said to her: "Do as you please, until he is weaned from the breast; and may the Lord fulfil all your request." And the woman stayed and nursed the child until he was weaned from the breast.
After that she went up to Shiloh. She took with her one [?] bullock, bread, and one measure of wheat flour, and they came to the temple of the Lord at Shiloh, and the child Samuel was with them.

They brought him before the Lord. His father slaughtered the bullock, and they offered the sacrifice according to the earlier custom by which they make offerings before the Lord. They presented the child to the Lord, for his father had slaughtered the bullock as a ransom for the child. And his mother brought the child to Eli the priest.
And she said: "I beseech you, my lord, as your soul lives: I am the woman who stood before you to offer my prayers before the Lord
for this child. And the Lord has granted me the request that I asked of him.
And behold, he shall stand before the Lord all the days of his life, to serve the Lord and to worship the Lord."
And Hannah said: "My heart is made strong by the Lord, and my horn is exalted by my God. My mouth is opened wide over my enemies; I have rejoiced in your salvation!
For there is no one holy like you, O Lord, and no one holy besides you, and no one righteous like God!
Do not boast, and do not speak lofty things beyond measure, and do not let arrogant words come out of your mouth! For God is the Lord of knowledge, and God prepares his own works.
The bows of the mighty have grown weak, and the weak have clothed themselves with strength.
Those who were sated have lacked bread, and the hungry have taken possession of the land; for the barren woman has borne seven children, and she who had many children has grown weak.
The Lord kills and makes alive; he casts down into hell and brings up again.
The Lord makes poor and makes rich; he humbles and exalts.
He raises the poor from the earth and lifts the fallen from the dunghill, to seat him with the mighty, with the mighty of his people, and he gives him thrones of glory to inherit.
He grants the request of those who ask of him and blesses the years of the righteous, for a man's might is no firm strength.

The Lord makes his adversaries weak; the Lord is holy! Let not the wise man boast in his wisdom, let not the mighty man boast in his strength, let not the rich man boast in his riches; but let him who boasts boast in this: in understanding and knowing the Lord, and in doing righteous judgment on the earth. The Lord has gone up into the heavens and thundered; he himself shall judge the ends of the earth in his righteousness. He will give strength to our king, and the Lord will exalt the horn of his anointed."
They left the child Samuel at Shiloh before the Lord, worshipped the Lord, and went to their home at Armathaim. And the child Samuel grew and served the Lord before Eli the priest.
And the sons of Eli, wicked and lawless offspring, who had no understanding of the fear of God,

And neither the custom of the priesthood, the custom of the people's offerings, was to be offered by the priest. Then one of the priest's servants would come to take up the meat, and in his hands he had a three-pronged fork.

And he would thrust it into the pan [?], or the pot, or the cauldron, and whatever first came up on the fork, he would carry that off for the priest. They did this to the sons of Israel who came to Shiloh to offer sacrifice to the Lord.

And before the fat had been burned before the Lord, the priest's servant would come and say to the man who was offering: "Give me meat to roast for the priest, and I will not take boiled meat from the cauldrons."

Then the man who had come to offer the sacrifice would say to him: "Let us first offer the incense and the sacrifice of the Lord, and after that take whatever you wish from all the offerings." But he would say to him: "No, give it to me now; if not, I will take whatever I want!"
And the sin of those sacrifices grew very great before the Lord, for they treated the sacrifices of the Lord with contempt.
And Samuel stood before the Lord, girded with the ephod.
And his mother would weave him a little robe made to his size, and she would bring it to him year by year, when she and her husband came to Shiloh to offer the sacrifice of the customary feasts.

And Eli blessed Elkanah and his wife Hannah, and said to him: "May the Lord raise up other offspring for you from your wife in return for the loan you gave to the Lord!" And Elkanah went to his own house.
And the Lord looked upon Hannah, and she bore three more sons and three daughters. And the boy Samuel grew and became very wise before the Lord.
And Eli was old, and he heard what his sons were doing to the sons of Israel, and also that his sons lay with the women who had taken refuge at the doors of the tent of testimony.
And Eli said to them: "What are these deeds of yours, this complaint about you that I hear from the people of the Lord?"
"No, children! Do not do this, for the report I hear about you is not good, for you are cooling the mind of this people so that they do not serve the Lord."

"If a man sins against a man, someone will pray for him to the Lord God; but if a man sins against the Lord God, to whom will they pray for him?" And they did not heed their father's voice, for the Lord willed to destroy them.
And the boy Samuel grew and grew strong before the Lord and before men.

And a man was sent to Eli, and he said to him: "Thus says the Lord: I clearly revealed myself to your father's house while they were still in the land of Egypt, in the house of Pharaoh, under the yoke of slavery.

And I chose your father's house out of all the tribes of Israel to be priests to me, to go up to my altar, to burn incense, and to carry my vessels of service before me. And I gave your father's house all the fire offerings of the sacrifices of the sons of Israel for food.

And why have you looked upon my altars and my sacrifices with a shameless eye, and honored your sons more than me, so that they might be glorified with the produce of my sacrifices which the sons of Israel offered to me?

Therefore thus says the Lord God of Israel: I said this: "Your house and the house of your father shall stand before me forever." And now, behold, the Lord says: Far be it from me; it is not so. I will never do that. Instead, I will glorify those who glorify me, and I will bring contempt on those who hold me in contempt.
Behold, the days are coming when I will cut off your descendants and the descendants of your father's house from my temple, for all the days of my life.
And I will establish a mighty labour [?] that will do good in every way to the house of Israel, and there shall no longer be an old man of yours in my house for all time.

I will not cut off every man of yours from my altar; he will remain to make your eyes waste away and to wear down [?] your head. And all the remnant of your father's house shall fall by the sword of enemies.
And this shall be the sign for you concerning these two sons of yours, Hophni and Phinehas: on a single day they shall fall by the edge of the sword.
And I will raise up for myself a faithful priest who will carry out all the will of my heart, and I will build him a sure house, and he shall walk before my anointed all the days of his life.

And all who are left of your house shall come and bow down to him for a single silver coin and a loaf of bread. They shall plead with him and say to him: "Put me into a priest's place, so that I may eat bread in the house of the Lord."
For the word of the Lord was rare in those days
And it happened in those days that Eli was sleeping in a certain place. His eyes had begun to grow heavy, and he could not see.
The lamp of God had not yet been lit, and Samuel was sleeping in the temple of the Lord, where the ark of the covenant stood.
And the Lord called Samuel and said to him: "Samuel, Samuel!" And Samuel answered and said: "Here I am, Lord."
And Samuel ran to Eli and said to him: "Why did you call me?" Eli said to him: "I did not call you. Go back to your place and sleep, my child." And Samuel went and slept in his place.

And the Lord called the boy again, a second time, and said to him: "Samuel, Samuel!" And Samuel was startled, and he ran to Eli and said to him: "Why did you call me?" And Eli said to him: "I did not call you, my child. Go back to your place and sleep"
Samuel did not know that this was a revelation from the Lord to him.
And the Lord called Samuel again, a third time. And Samuel got up and ran to Eli and said to him: "Here I am. Why did you call me?" And Eli understood that it was the Lord who was calling him.
And he said to him: "Go back to your place and sleep, my child. And if he calls you again, say to him: 'Your servant is listening; speak, Lord.'" And Samuel went and slept in his place.
And the Lord came and stood over him and said to him, as before: "Samuel, Samuel!" Samuel answered and said: "Let the Lord speak, for your servant is listening."
And the Lord said to Samuel: "Behold, I am about to fulfil all my words against Israel. Both ears of everyone who hears of it will ring.
On that day I will bring upon Eli everything that I have spoken, and I will lay it upon his whole house, and I will carry it through to the end."
And he told him about the iniquities of his sons, for his sons spoke evil against God, and he did not correct them.
But I did not promise this: that I would forgive the iniquities of the house of Eli through sacrifice and incense, for all time to come.
And Samuel slept there until morning. He rose early at dawn and opened the doors of the temple. And Samuel did not dare to tell Eli the vision, because he was afraid on account of what he had seen.
Eli called to Samuel and said, "My son!" And he said, "Here I am."
Eli said to him, "Tell me the word that came to you this night, and do not hide even one word from me! May the Lord do this and that to you, and add more to it, if you hide even one word from me."
Then Samuel told him everything the Lord had spoken to him, and did not hide even one word from him. And Eli said, "May the Lord do whatever is pleasing to him, for he alone is the Lord."
And Samuel grew strong, and the Lord was with him; and of all his words, not one word fell to the ground.
And all Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, knew that Samuel was a trustworthy prophet of the Lord.

The Lord made himself known to Samuel in Shiloh, when the Lord appeared according to the word of the Lord. And Samuel was trusted throughout all Israel, from one end of the land to the other. And Eli was very old, and his sons walked in the way of iniquity before the Lord.
And in those days the Philistines gathered to fight against Israel. The Israelites prepared for battle; they came and camped at Ebenezer, and the Philistines camped at Aphek.
And a great battle broke out between them, and Israel was defeated. And the Philistines struck down in the battle about four hundred men.

And the rest of the people of Israel were routed and came back into their camp. And the elders of Israel took counsel among themselves: "Why has the Lord given us up today before the Philistines? Now come, let us bring the ark of the covenant of the Lord our God from Shiloh and carry it before us, and let us defeat our enemies."
Then they brought out the ark of the covenant, for the cherubim stood with the ark; and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, came down with the ark of the covenant.
And when they brought the ark of the covenant of the Lord into the camp, the Israelites saw it and shouted with a great voice, and the earth resounded.

When the Philistines heard this, they trembled and said to one another, "What is this sound of shouting in the camp of the Hebrews?" And they all learned that the ark of the covenant had come into their camp.

And they were very afraid and said to one another, "Woe to us, for their God has come to help them!" And they said, "Lord, deliver us from their hands, for this terrible sound was not among them yesterday or the day before."
"Woe to us! Who will deliver us from the hands of the God of this mighty people? This is the God who struck the land of Egypt with plague, and [in?] the wilderness."

Then they began to encourage one another and said, "Be strong, you Philistines, and let us not become subject to the Hebrews as they have served us. Be brave and fight!" And the Philistines took heart.
And they fought and won, and Israel was defeated by the Philistines, and Israel fled to its camp. The slaughter was great: thirty thousand armed men of Israel fell.
And they carried off the Ark of the Law, and both sons of Eli fell by the sword.
And a man of Benjamin fled from the battle line and came to Shiloh with his tunic torn and earth poured over his head.

And Eli the priest was sitting at the gates of the city, watching the road, because he was anxious for the Ark of God. And the man had only just arrived to tell the news in the city, and he was telling it to the townspeople.
When Eli heard the noise, he asked them and said to them, "What is that noise?" And at that very word the messenger [?] arrived and told him everything that had happened.
And Eli was old, for he was ninety-eight years old, and his eyes had become fixed and he could not see. Eli asked the men and said to them, "What is this noise of uproar?"
And the man said to him, "I am the one who has come from the camp of the Israelites, having fled." Eli answered and said to him, "And what has happened, my son?"

He told him and said, "Israel has been defeated by the Philistines, and every fighting man has been put to flight and has fallen to death by the sword, and both your sons have been killed, and they have carried off the holy Ark of the Law."

And when Eli heard this, the carrying off of the Ark, he fell backward from his seat and fell straight backward [?] onto the threshold, and his back was broken and he died; he was old and aged. And he had labored [?] for Israel only forty years.

And his son's wife, the wife of Phinehas, was pregnant. When she heard this news, that the Ark had been captured and that her husband and her father-in-law had died, she began to weep and lament, and at once labor came upon her; she gave birth and died.
And the women who were standing by her said to her, "Do not be afraid, for you have borne a son!" But she answered nothing, for she had grown weak.
And they called the child by the name Vaibariakibel [Ichabod], because of the Ark of the Law and because of her father-in-law and her husband, for they had died.
They began to speak and said, "The glory has been taken from us by the Lord."
For the Philistines carried off the Ark of the Law of God from Ebenezer to Ashdod.
And they brought it into the house of Dagon and set it up next to Dagon.

And the people of Ashdod rose early and went into the house of Dagon, and they saw Dagon, that he had fallen on his face on the ground before the Ark of the Lord. And they raised Dagon up and set him back in his own place.

And again on the next morning they saw Dagon fallen on his face before the Ark of God, and Dagon's head and both his hands and his claws [?] had been broken off [?]; only his trunk was left on the threshold.
For this reason the priests of Dagon and everyone who enters the house of Dagon in Ashdod do not set foot on the threshold, but step over it with a stride, to this very day.

And the hand of the Lord grew heavy upon the people of Ashdod, and he struck them with the disease of tumors [?], and he multiplied mice among them, and their watering places [?], their fields and their quarters were filled with mice, and death increased throughout their city.

And when the people of Ashdod saw that these days had come upon them, they spoke to one another and said, "It is not right for this Ark of God to remain among us, for he has become angry with us and with our god Dagon."

And the people of Ashdod summoned the ruler of the Philistines and said to him: "What shall we do with this ark of the God of Israel?" The people of Gath answered and said: "Give it to us!" And they carried the ark of God away to Gath.

And when they had carried the ark to Gath, the hand of the Lord was upon the city of the people of Gath, and death increased among them. He struck them with the plague of the [?] (perhaps "hinder parts"), from the least of them to the greatest. And the people of Gath made for themselves golden [?] (perhaps "tumor figures"), for mice had multiplied among them.
And they carried the ark of the God of Israel away to Ashkelon. When the ark arrived, the people of Ashkelon said: "Why have you brought the ark here to destroy us?"
And the ark of God stayed in the land of the Philistines for only seven months, and mice multiplied in their land.
And the Philistines sent for the priests and the diviners and said to them: "What shall we do with this ark of God? Tell us how we may send it back to its own place."

And they said to them: "If you send away the ark of the Lord, do not send it away like that. Send a gift to him along with it on account of your plague, and you will be relieved. Otherwise he will not lift his hand, which weighs heavily upon you."

They answered and said: "And what shall we give for our healing?" And they said: "Make five golden [?] (perhaps "tumor figures"), one for each of your number, for there is sin among you and among this people of yours.

And make five golden mice in the likeness of the mice that ravaged your land, and give glory to the God of Israel, so that he may take the plague away from you and lift his mighty hand from you, from your gods and from your land.
Why do you harden your hearts, as the Egyptians and Pharaoh hardened their hearts? He struck them with this severe plague, and only then did they let the people go, and they departed.
So now make a new cart, and yoke to it two milk cows that have calved for the first time and have never been yoked [?], and keep their calves back.
And set the ark of the covenant of the Lord on the cart, and send the golden objects along with it. Put them in a linen cloth and place them at its side. Then let it go, and you follow behind it.

And watch: if it goes toward its own borders, in the direction of Beth-shemesh, then you will know that he has sent this plague upon us. If it does not go, you will know that his hand has not harmed us, and that this sickness came upon us by some chance."

And the Philistines did so. They took the milk cows that had calved for the first time and had never been yoked [?], and yoked them to the cart, and kept their calves at home. And they sent word to them, saying: "The Philistines have brought the ark of the covenant of the Lord here. Now come and take it for yourselves."
And they placed the ark of God on the cart, along with the golden mice and the [?] (perhaps "tumor figures"). They put these in a linen cloth and placed them at its side.

And the cows went along the road toward Beth-shemesh. They kept to the straight road and turned aside neither to the right nor to the left. And the rulers of the Philistines followed behind them as far as the border of Beth-shemesh.
And there were some people there in Beth-shemesh. When the reapers saw the ark of God, they rejoiced greatly and went out to meet it.
And the cart came and stood beside the great stone. They broke up the cart, slaughtered the cows and offered them as a sacrifice to the Lord.

And the Levites took up the ark of the Lord, and the linen cloth [?] and the golden vessels, and set them on the great stone. And the people of Beth-shemesh offered sacrifice to the Lord God on that day.
And the five lords of the Philistines saw this and went back to Ashkelon.

And these are the golden tumours that the Philistines had made to the Lord for their relief: one for the people of Ashdod, one for the people of Gaza, one for the people of Ashkelon, one for the people of Ekron, one for the people of Gath.

Likewise the golden mice, matching the number of the cities, the cities of the five lords, the fortified cities [?], as far as the village of the Perizzite and as far as the great stone. On that stone they set the ark of the law of the Lord, which stood in the field of Joshua of Beth-shemesh.

And the sons of Jeconiah did not join with the men of Beth-shemesh when they saw the ark of the law of the Lord. And God struck down fifty thousand and seventy of their men. And the people began to mourn, because the Lord had struck them with a great blow.
And the men of Beth-shemesh said: "Who is able to stand before the face of the Lord, the Holy One? And to whom shall this ark of the Lord go?"
And they sent messengers to Kiri[?]

And the people of Kiriath-jearim took the ark of the law of the Lord and brought it into the house of Abinadab, which was built on the hill. And they chose his son Eleazar and appointed him keeper of the ark of the Lord.
And from the time they brought the ark of God to Kiriath-jearim, the time grew long and came to about twenty years. And Israel turned to the Lord on that day.
And Samuel said to all Israel: "If you turn to the Lord with all your heart, and put away idolatry and serve the Lord God, he will deliver you from the hands of the Philistines."
And the sons of Israel heard the word. They threw away the Baals, the sacred groves [?] and the idol of Ashtaroth, and they served the Lord God.
And Samuel said to them: "Gather all the people of Israel to Mizpah, and we will pray to the Lord for you."

And all the people gathered at Mizpah. They drew water and poured it out on the ground before the Lord, and they fasted on that day and said: "We have sinned before the Lord." For Samuel was judging the sons of Israel at Mizpah.
And the Philistines heard that the sons of Israel had gathered at Mizpah, and the Philistines also gathered and came against Israel. When the sons of Israel heard this, they were very much afraid.
And they said to Samuel: "Do not stop praying to the Lord for us, so that he may deliver us from the hands of the Philistines." And Samuel said: "I will not stop praying to the Lord for you."
Samuel took one suckling lamb and offered it as a sacrifice before the Lord for all the people of Israel. And the Lord heard Samuel's request.
And while Samuel was offering the sacrifice, the Philistines were just then approaching, ready to fight against Israel. And the Lord thundered against the Philis-

-tines with a crashing sound. And they were terrified and were defeated before the Israelites. And the Israelites came out of Mizpah, pursued and overtook the Philistines and slaughtered them, and they put the rest to flight as far as Bethor.
And Samuel took a stone and set it up between Mizpah and the place of battle array, and he named it Ebenezer, which translated means "stone of help," for he said, "Until now the Lord has helped us."
And he humbled the Philistines, and they did not again go up against Israel. And the hand of the Lord was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel.

And they took back the cities that the Philistines had taken from the sons of Israel, from Ashkelon as far as Gath, and they took back the territory of Israel from the hands of the Philistines. And there was peace between Israel and the Amorites.
And Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.
And Samuel would go year after year on a circuit around Bethel and Gilgal and Mizpah, and Samuel judged Israel in all the holy places of Israel.
And he would come back to Ramah, for his home was there, and there he would judge Israel. And Samuel built an altar to the Lord God there.
And when Samuel grew old, he appointed his sons as judges over Israel.
And these are the names of his sons: his firstborn was Joel, and the next was Abiron. They were judges in Beersheba.
His sons did not walk in his ways. Instead they went after gain, took bribes, and did not do justice.
And all the tribes of Israel gathered and came to Samuel at Ramah.
And they said to him, "You have grown old, and your sons do not walk in your ways. Now give us a king to judge us justly, as the other nations have."
And this word displeased Samuel, because they said to him, "Give us a king who will lead us." And Samuel prayed to the Lord.
And the Lord said to him, "Listen to the word of this people, for it is not you in any way that they have rejected, when you were king over them,
in all their deeds, from the time I brought them out of Egypt until this very day. For they have forsaken me and served foreign idols, and so they have done to you as well.
Now listen to them, and set a covenant among them, and tell them the custom and law of the kingship of the one who will reign over them."
And Samuel told all the words of God to the people who were asking him for a king.
And he said to them, "This will be the custom of the king who will reign over them: he will demand your children and make them horsemen, and some of them charioteers and runners before him,
and he will appoint some as commanders of thousands, as plowmen and reapers, as vinedressers and grape-harvesters. And he will make some of them makers of chain mail and of weapons.
And he will take your daughters and make them perfumers, cooks and bakers.
And he will take your fields and your vineyards and your olive groves, the very best and most fruitful, and give them to his servants.
And from the produce of your fields and vineyards he will take a tenth for his eunuchs and servants.
And he will take your menservants and maidservants, your [?] and [?] and your oxen, and set them to the king's work.
And he will take a tenth of your flocks, and you will be his slaves and servants.
And you will cry out to that king, and the Lord will not hear you, because you yourselves chose the king."
But the people would not listen to Samuel's words. Then they said to him, "It is not so. Set a king over us."
and we will be obedient to him, like the other nations, and he will judge us and fight our enemies."
Then Samuel heard those words of theirs and told them all to the Lord God.
And the Lord said to Samuel, "Listen to them, and set a king over them to reign over them." And Samuel went out and commanded the people, "Go, each of you, to his own city."
And there was a man there of the tribe of Benjamin, and his name was Kish, son of Abiel, son of Sabiga, son of Bakhe, son of Aphek, a Jeminite. And that man was mighty.
And he had a son, whose name was Saul, and he was tall in stature and handsome. And there was no one in Israel taller in stature than he, for from his shoulders up he was taller than any man.
And his father's donkeys were lost, and Kish said to his son Saul, "Take one young man with you; go and search for those donkeys!" And they went and crossed the hill country of Ephraim.

And they went around the mountains of Sair and did not find them, and they went around all the land of Salim and did not find them; and they came to the land of the Jeminites, and did not find them there either.
Then they came to Zuph, and Saul said to the young man, "Come, let us turn back to our father, lest he leave off caring about the donkeys and become anxious about us."

The young man answered and said, "I have heard that there is a man of God here, in this city, honored and glorious, and whatever he says all comes to pass. Now let us go to him, so that we may ask him which direction is best, and then we will go on."
Saul answered the young man and said, "Let us go then; but what shall we bring to the man of God? For even the bread from our provisions has run out, and we have nothing more than what you see."
The young man answered Saul again and said, "I have here with me a quarter of a shekel of silver. Take it and give it to the man of God, so that he may tell us our way, the one we should go by."

For formerly in the land of Israel those who went to inquire of the Lord through the man of God used to say this about him: "Let us go to the man who is the seer"; for in those times they called the prophet a seer.
Then Saul said to the young man, "Good, come, let us go!" And they went to the city where the man of God was.
As they reached the entrance of the city, they met some girls who were coming out to draw water, and they said to them, "Is the seer here?"
The girls answered and said, "He has just now come into the city ahead of you, for he has come to offer a sacrifice at the high place.

And when you enter the city, you will find him right away, and the people assembled, for they are waiting for him and will not eat bread until he has offered the sacrifices to the Lord, and only then will they eat bread. And now go up quickly, and you will find him in the city, for today he has come for this, to offer the sacrifice."
And as they went into the middle of the city, Samuel met them, for he was going up to the high place.
For God had revealed it to Samuel one day before, before Saul had yet met him, and the Lord said to him:

"Tomorrow at this hour I will send to you a man from the land of Benjamin. Anoint him king over my people Israel, and he will save my people Israel from the hands of the foreigners, for I have looked upon the humiliation of my people, because their cry has come to me."
And when Samuel saw Saul, the Lord said to him: "This is the man of whom I spoke to you. He shall reign over my people."
And Saul said to Samuel: "Tell me the name of the seer."

Samuel answered and said to him: "I myself am he. Go up ahead of me to the high place, and eat bread with me today. Tomorrow I will send you away and tell you everything that is the desire of your heart.

As for the asses, do not worry about them at all, for it is three days today, since the asses have been found. From now on think of good things, for who in Israel has such joy today as you and your father's house? Now go up ahead of me to the high place."

Saul answered and said: "Am I not the son of a Jeminite man, the least among the kindreds of Israel, and is not my clan the smallest of all the clans of Benjamin? Why then, my lord, have you said this word to me?"
And Samuel took Saul and the young man who was with him, brought them into his lodging, and ordered him to sit at the head, above the seventy guests.
And he said to the cook: "Bring me the portion that I gave you to set aside."
And the cook brought one thigh together with the [?], and Samuel said to Saul: "Behold, this is a testimony for you before all those people!" And Saul took it and ate it with Samuel on that day.
And they came down from the high place to the city of Benjamin, and they set up a bed for him on the roof.

And he lay down. And as dawn was breaking, Samuel called down to Saul on the roof and said to him: "Get up and come down, and I will send you on your way!" And Saul got up, and the two of them went out of the city.

And they came to the edge of the city, and Samuel said to Saul: "Tell that young man to go on ahead of us, and you stand still and hear the command of the Lord." And Saul said to the young man: "Go on ahead!"

And when the young man had gone on, Samuel took the horn of anointing oil and poured it on his head, and kissed him and said to him: "The Lord has anointed you king over his people Israel. You shall lead the people of the Lord and save them from the hands of their enemies! And this shall be a sign to you that the Lord your God has anointed you and set you over his inheritance.

And this shall be a sign to you: when you go away from me today, two men will meet you there by the tomb of Rachel, at the border of Benjamin, about noon. They will begin to walk before you and will tell you: 'We have found the asses that you were looking for, and your father has forgotten his concern for the asses and is worried about you, saying: What has become of my son?'

And when you have gone on a little, near the beautiful oak, three men going up to Bethel will meet you there: one will have three young goats, one will have wine in a skin, and one will have a basket full of bread.
And they will greet you in peace and hand things to you and say to you: 'Take a portion of this, and receive a portion of all this.'

And after this you will go up to the hill of God, where the offering of the Philistines is, and there a hundred Philistines will meet you. And when you enter the city, a band of prophets will meet you coming down from Bamah, and in front of them singers with timbrel and lyre, pipe and drum, and they will be prophesying.
And the Spirit of God will come upon you, and you too will prophesy with them, and you will be changed into a new man.
And when all these signs have been fulfilled for you, do whatever you wish, for God is with you.
Now go down ahead of me to Gilgal, and I will come there to offer the sacrifices of the altar and the peace offerings. Wait for me seven days, until I come to you and tell you what you are to do.
And as he turned and turned his back to go away from Samuel, God changed his heart and renewed it. And all these signs that Samuel had told him came upon him on that same day.
And he came to Bamah, to the hill, and the bands of prophets came to meet him, and the Spirit of God spread over him, and he too began to prophesy among them.

And when they saw this, those who had seen him the day before yesterday and earlier, that he had not prophesied among the prophets, [said:] And what then [?] has happened to the son of Kish? Is Saul now also among the prophets?
One of them answered and said: And who is his father? For this reason this saying became a proverb: Is Saul too among the prophets?
And he came to Bamah, just to the hill.
And his uncle said to the young man: Where did you go? And he said to him: To look for the donkeys, and we did not find them anywhere, so we went to Samuel.
And he told us that the donkeys had been found. But he did not reveal to him what Samuel had told him about the kingship.
And Samuel gathered all the people to Mizpah.
And he said to the sons of Israel: Thus says the Lord God: I brought the sons of Israel out of the land of Egypt and delivered you from the hands of Pharaoh, who oppressed you.

But today you have despised your God, who was your deliverer from every affliction and evil, and you said: Set a king over us. Now then, present yourselves before the Lord, tribe by tribe and by your thousands.
And Samuel brought together all the tribes of Israel and cast lots, and the lot fell on Benjamin.

And he brought together the families of Benjamin and cast lots, and the lot fell on Matri. And he brought together the family of Matri man by man and cast lots, and the lot fell on Saul son of Kish. And they looked for him and did not find him.
And Samuel inquired of the Lord and said: Is the man perhaps somewhere among us? And the Lord said to Samuel: Look, he is hidden among the baggage.
And Samuel ran and brought Saul out from there and set him among them, and he was taller than all the people from the shoulders up.
Then Samuel said to all the people: See, there is no one among you like him in any way. And all the people saw and said: Long live the king forever!

And Samuel spoke to all his people and set out the whole ordinance of the kingship, and he wrote it in a book and laid it before the Lord. And he dismissed all the people, and they went, each to his own place.
And Saul went to his house, which was in Gibeah. And some sons of the mighty stepped forward, whose hearts the Lord had stirred toward Saul.
But the sons of lawlessness despised Saul and said, "How will Saul save us?" And they brought him no gift at all. But he kept silent and said nothing.

And about a month later, Nahash the Ammonite came with his people and surrounded Jabesh. And the men of Jabesh said to Nahash the Ammonite, "Make a covenant with us and set an agreement between us, and we will serve you."

Nahash the Ammonite answered them and said, "What covenant shall I make with you, except this: the gouging out of your right eyes. Let that be the covenant between us, and let it be a reproach upon Israel forever."
And the men of Jabesh said to him, "Give us a respite of just seven days, so that we may send messengers to all the borders of Israel. And if there is no one to help us, we will come out to you."
And the messengers of Jabesh came to Gibeah, where Saul was, and told this message to all the people. And all the people wept and lamented.
And the next day, right at dawn, Saul arrived, driving oxen in from the field, and he said, "What is it? Why are you weeping?" Then they told him the whole message of the men of Jabesh.
And the Spirit of God came upon Saul, and he became very angry at their words.

And he took the two oxen, slaughtered them, cut them up limb by limb, and sent them around to all the tribes of Israel by the hand of messengers, saying, "The struggle of war has come upon us. Now every man who does not come out to battle following Saul and Samuel will have his cattle and sheep cut up just like this." And a great fear from the Lord fell upon all the people of Israel, and all the people cried out as with one voice and gathered to Saul.
And Saul reviewed the people by muster. Those who came at the time of the muster were about six thousand men from the house of Israel, and those of the house of Judah were about seventy thousand men.

And Saul said to the messengers who had come, "Tell the men of Jabesh-gilead this: 'Tomorrow your deliverance will come, as soon as the sun grows hot.'" And the messengers went to Jabesh-gilead and told the message to all the men of the city, and they rejoiced greatly.
And the men of Jabesh said to Nahash, "Tomorrow we will come out to you, and you may do to us whatever pleases you."

And the next day Saul came and divided the people into three companies. He fell upon the camp of the Ammonites at the very hour of dawn, and they struck down the whole camp of the Ammonites until the sun grew hot. And the survivors were scattered in flight, each one by himself, and not even two were left together.
Then the people said to Samuel, "Who were the men who said, 'Saul shall not reign over us'? Hand those men over to us, and we will put them to death right now."
Saul answered and said, "No one shall die here today, not a single man, for today the Lord has brought about his salvation in Israel."
Samuel began to speak to the people and said: "Come, let us go into Gilgal and renew his kingship there."

And all the people gathered went to Gilgal, and there Samuel anointed Saul king before the Lord in Gilgal. And there they offered sacrifices of peace offerings to the Lord, and Samuel and Saul and all the people of Israel rejoiced.
Then Samuel said to the people: "Behold, I have listened to you and have set a king over you, as you asked."
"Now there is your king before you! And I have grown old, and my sons are among you from their youth; and you yourselves know that I have laboured before you from my youth until this very day."

"Now bear witness against me before the Lord and before his anointed: if I have taken from anyone a calf or a single [?], or if I have seized anything belonging to any of you, or if I have oppressed anyone in anything, or if I have snatched anything out of anyone's hands, whether a garment or a sandal, or if I have ever let my eyes loose upon you, bear witness against me before the Lord, and I will repay you all of it."
Then all the people answered and said: "You have never oppressed any of us in anything, nor have you seized anything from us, nor have you taken anything from anyone out of our hands."

Samuel answered the people and said: "May the Lord be witness among you, and may his anointed be witness, that you have found nothing evil in me." All the people answered and said: "Yes, may he be witness!"
And Samuel said: "May the Lord God of Israel be witness, who made Moses and Aaron, who brought the children of Israel, our fathers, out of the land of the Egyptians; he himself is witness."
"Now stand before me, and I will show you judgement before the Lord, and I will tell you the righteous judgement of the Lord and all that he did for us and for our fathers."

"At the time when Jacob and his sons went into the land of Egypt, and when the Egyptians oppressed them, and our fathers cried out to the Lord, the Lord God sent Moses and Aaron, and he brought our fathers out of the land of Egypt and settled them in this place."
"But they forgot the Lord their God, and he gave them into the hands of Sisera, king of the Assyrians, and into the hands of the king of the Moabites, and they did them harm."

"And they cried out to the Lord and said: 'We have sinned before you, O Lord, for we have forsaken you, the Lord our God, and we served the Baalim and the groves of Astaroth. Now deliver us from the hands of our enemies, and we will serve you.'"
"And the Lord God sent Jeroboam and Barak and Jephthah and Samuel, and the Lord delivered you from the hands of your enemies who were round about you, and he settled you in peace and in hope."
"But now, when you saw that Nahash, king of the children of Ammon, was coming against you, you said to me: 'Set a king over us!' Yet our God is our king."
"And now, behold, there is your king, whom you chose and asked for, whom the Lord your God has given you."

"And if you fear the Lord and serve him and obey his commandments and do not rise up against his words in rebellion, and you and your king are obedient to his commandments, then he will be your keeper..."

If you do not listen to the command of the Lord your God, and rise up in rebellion against his commandments, the hand of the Lord will be against you and against your king, and the Lord will destroy you.
But now, all the more, submit and stand still before these great things of the Lord, which the Lord will do before your eyes.

Is it not now the wheat harvest? And if you wish, I will ask the Lord, and he will give you a violent rain, full of thunder, and you will understand that your wickedness has grown great before the Lord, because you asked for a king.
And Samuel asked the Lord, and the Lord gave him a violent rain, full of terrible thunder. And all Israel greatly feared the Lord, and Samuel.
And all the people said to Samuel: "Pray to the Lord your God for these your servants, so that we may not perish today, for we have added to our sins by asking for a king for ourselves."
Samuel answered the people and said: "Do not be afraid. Even though this wickedness has come from you, do not turn aside from the ways of the Lord, but serve the Lord with all your heart.
And do not follow worthless things, which have not profited you and have not saved you, for they are worthless.
But the Lord will not cast away his people, for the sake of his great name, for the Lord has received you and chosen you to be a treasured people.
As for me, far be it from me to sin against the Lord by failing to pray to the Lord for you, and by failing to teach you the way of righteousness and uprightness.
But you must fear the Lord and serve him in truth and with all your heart, for you have seen how greatly the Lord has acted among you.
If you speak evil, you and your crowned ones, you will perish in your lawlessness."
Saul was one year old when he became king, and in the second year of his reign over Israel

Saul chose three thousand men of the sons of Israel for himself. Two thousand were with Saul at Michmash, and the other thousand were with Jonathan on the mountain of Bethel, on the hill of Gibeon of Benjamin. He sent the rest of the people away, each to his own place.

And after this Jonathan struck down the detached company of the Philistines that was on the hill. The foreigners heard of this, and Saul ordered the trumpet to be blown throughout all the land, and said: "Let all the land of the Hebrews know that the servants have revolted."
And all Israel learned that Saul had struck down and slain the company of the foreigners, and the Israelites had become loathsome to the foreigners. And all the people gathered to Saul at Gilgal.

And the foreigners assembled and went to fight against Israel with three thousand chariots and six thousand horsemen, and the rest of the people were without number, like the sand on the seashore. They went up and camped at Michmash, behind Beth-horon.
And when the men of Israel saw that the foreigners were pressing hard on them, they withdrew and hid in caves and in clefts of the rocks, in pits and in water cisterns.
And some crossed over into the land of Gad and Gilead. All the people scattered away from him, and Saul was left alone at Gilgal.

He stood and waited seven days, according to the appointment set by Samuel, and Samuel had not yet come to Gilgal. Saul began to speak and said: “Samuel has not come to Gilgal, and this people has scattered from me.”
“Now bring me some of the offerings, and I will offer the sacrifice of the peace offering.”
And just as he had offered that sacrifice, Samuel arrived, and Saul went out to meet Samuel, so that Samuel might bless him.

Samuel said to Saul: “What have you done?” Saul answered and said to him: “When I saw that the people had scattered from me, and you delayed and did not come according to the promise that you made with me, and the Philistines had come to Michmash,
I said: ‘The Philistines must not come down on me at Gilgal while I have not yet entreated [?] the Lord.’ So I purified myself and offered this sacrifice.”
Then Samuel said to Saul: “That sacrifice of yours was in vain, because you did not keep the commandments of the Lord. By them your kingdom would have been established over Israel for all time.

But now that kingdom of yours will not remain with you. The Lord will seek out a man pleasing to his heart and will appoint him ruler over his people, because you did not keep the commandment that the Lord commanded you.”

And Samuel went his way from Gilgal, and the rest of the people went up with Saul to meet the army drawn up for battle. And when they came to Geba, the hill of Benjamin, Saul reviewed his people who were with him, and about six hundred men were found there.
And Saul, his son Jonathan and the people who were with him sat down in Gibeon of Benjamin and wept. And the Philistines encamped at Michmash.
And the raiders who went out from the Philistines divided into three companies. One company set out toward Gophor, by the road of the spring, from Sogalim.
Another company headed along the road to Beth-horon, and the third company went to Gibeon, which leads down to the valley of Saba, which lies toward the wilderness.

And at that time no ironsmith was to be found in the land of Israel, for the Philistines had said: “The Hebrews must not make spears, swords, mail or any weapon at all, and come into our land without fear.”

Instead, the Israelites would go down to the land of the Philistines, each of them to have his own working tool forged: ploughshare, sickle, scythe, axe and pruning knife. And the Philistines would do the work for payment.
And only when the harvest was over would they pay them: three measures for a ploughshare, axe, scythe, sickle or pruning knife, and they would also add a goad.

And in the days of the battle at Michmash there was no sword at all, no sabre and no spear in the hands of the people who were with Saul and Jonathan. Only Saul and Jonathan had a sword, and even that had been forged by the Philistines.

And one day Jonathan, the son of Saul, said to his servant who carried his bow and quiver: “Come, let us cross over to the camp of the uncircumcised, which is opposite us.” And his father Saul did not know that Jonathan was going out against the Philistines.
And Saul was sitting on the hill under a pomegranate tree at Magdos, and only six hundred men were with him.

And there was Ahijah, son of Ahitub, the brother of Ichabod, son of Phinehas, son of Eli, the high priest of Shiloh; he had the priestly vestment. And none of the people knew that Jonathan had crossed over toward the enemy.

And he had crossed over and was watching for a chance to attack the enemy at their way in and way out. And there were two rocky crags there, one on that side and one on this side. The name of one crag was Bozez and the name of the other Seneh.
The one crag stood to the north, by Michmash, and the other crag stood to the south, by Gibeon.

And Jonathan said to his servant, who carried his armor: "Come, let us cross over to the camp of the uncircumcised with the help of our God. For it is easy before God to save us from our enemies, whether with few people or with many."
Then the servant who carried his armor said to him: "Go on, do quickly whatever you wish. Behold, I am with you. As your heart is, so is mine. I will follow you."
Jonathan said: "Behold, we will cross over and creep up on them."
"If any of them says to us, 'Stand there a moment, and I will see what sort of men you are,' then let us stay where we are."
"But if they say, 'Come up to us,' let us go up against them openly. Then know that the Lord has handed them over into our hands. And let this be a sign for us."
And the two of them went into the camp of the foreigners. The foreigners began to talk and said: "Do you see those Hebrews, how they are coming out of their holes, where they had hidden from us?"

And the foreigners called from there to Jonathan: "Come, make your way up, and I will show you what you ought to learn from us." Then Jonathan said to the man who carried his armor: "Follow me! Now I know that the Lord God has handed them over into our hands."
And Jonathan climbed up on his hands and feet, and the young man with him, and they rushed upon them. When the foreigners saw Jonathan coming up against them, they rose up and went out to meet him.
And in that first clash, in [?], Jonathan cut down twenty [?] men, and the one who carried his armor was helping with his sword [?].

And those who stood against him were crushed. And the camp and those who were gathered round about were all being crushed together. And no man had the heart to fight, and the whole land was afraid, and a trembling from the Lord came upon them.
And Saul's watchmen, who were in Gibeah of Benjamin, saw the uproar in the camp of the foreigners. King Saul also learned of it, for he too was sitting on a height and was watching their uproar.

Saul spoke and said to the people who were with him: "Make a search and see whether any of us has crossed over there." And when they looked, they did not find Jonathan and his armor-bearer, who carried his bow and quiver.
And Saul said to Ahijah the high priest: "Spread out that ephod and inquire of the Lord."

And while Saul was still speaking to the high priest, the uproar among the foreigners kept growing stronger. And Saul said to Ahijah the high priest: "Draw back your hands and stop inquiring with that ephod."

And Saul rode out, and all the people with him, and they came to the place of battle. The Philistines had turned on one another: each man's sword was against his neighbour's head, and there was a very great rout.
And Saul's servants, who had fled from the Philistines, came and joined the people of the Israelites there, with Saul and with Jonathan.
And all who had been hiding in the hill country of Ephraim came and joined in the fighting against those who were fleeing.

And the Lord saved Israel on that day from the hands of the Philistines. The battle went from Michmash to Beth-horon, and with Saul were about ten thousand men of Israel. The fighting spread across the whole city and the hills of Ephraim.

At that time Saul acted foolishly, out of great ignorance, for he held fast his foot [?] and laid a curse on the people, saying: "Cursed be any man who eats bread before evening, until I have fully taken vengeance on my enemies." And no one ate bread that day.
And the whole land was feasting at the meal. There was a wood there, and there were a great many bees.
And all the people went into it, but no one dared to eat the honey, because they were afraid of the curse.

But Jonathan did not know about his father's curse. When Jonathan came to the place where the honey was, he put out the tip of his staff, dipped it into the honeycomb, and put it to his mouth. His eyes brightened and he grew strong.
One of the people answered him and said: "Your father bound the people with an oath, saying, 'Cursed be the man who eats bread today before evening.' And now every man is exhausted."
When Jonathan heard this, he was grieved and said: "My father has brought ruin on the whole land. I tasted only a little of this honey, and my eyes brightened and I grew strong.

So if only the people had eaten from the spoil taken from the enemy, they would have done the enemy more harm, and the blow struck among the Philistines today would have been greater than the one at Michmash.
And now, look, they are all exhausted." Then, when [?] had worn the people out and they were suffering from hunger,
all the people rushed on the spoil. They cut down sheep and oxen, slaughtered them, and ate the meat all mixed together with the blood.

Then the king was told: "The people have sinned against the Lord, because they have eaten meat with the blood." When Saul heard this, he was angry with the people and said: "You have broken the law and sinned! Now roll a large stone over to me and set it up."

And he told all the people that each man was to bring his own ox and sheep: "Slaughter them on this stone and offer them to God, and then eat, so that you no longer sin against the Lord your God by eating blood with the meat. Eat only the meat!" And the people did as the king had commanded them.
And Saul built an altar there to the Lord his God.

Saul spoke to the people and said: "Come [?], let us go down against the Philistines tonight, cut them down until daybreak, and destroy them completely." The people answered him: "Do whatever seems good to you!" The high priest answered and said: "Let us first inquire of the Lord, and only then go down against them."
And Saul stood up to inquire of the Lord and said: "Will you deliver them into my hands?" And the Lord did not answer him.
And Saul commanded all the people to gather before him, and he said to them: "Inquire and find out from whom this sin has come today,
for as the Lord lives, who saved Israel, even if this sin should be from Jonathan my son, I will surely put him to death!" And no one dared to answer him a word.

Then Saul said to the people: "Behold, we are all one. Now all of you stand on one side, and I and Jonathan my son on the other side, and let us cast lots, so that we may know whose it is." All the people answered and said: "Whatever is pleasing in your sight, do that."

Saul began to speak to the Lord and said: "O Lord God of Israel! Why is it that you did not answer your servant a word today? Is this iniquity from me or from Jonathan my son? Make it known to me, O Lord, by your own means. If it is from the people, show mercy."

And Saul, Jonathan and the people cast lots, and the lot of Jonathan came up. The people answered and said to Saul: "Far be it that Jonathan should die!" But Saul did not heed the words of the people.

Saul answered Jonathan and said: "Tell me quickly what you have done!" Jonathan answered Saul and said: "With the tip of the spear that is in my hand I tasted some of that honey from the honeycomb, for I did not know of your curse. And now, behold, I am to die."
Saul answered and said: "May the Lord do so and so to me if I do not put you to death!"

Then the people said to Saul: "Far be it, lord, that Jonathan should die today, for through him salvation has come about in Israel. Let there be pardon; as the Lord lives, not one hair of Jonathan's head shall fall to the ground!" The people prayed for Jonathan on that day, and Jonathan was saved from death.
Then they mounted and armed themselves and pursued after the Philistines, and they shut them up, each in his own place.

And Saul's kingship was established over Israel, and he fought against all his enemies: against Moab, the Ammonites, the Edomites, the Bethorites [?], the kings of Zobah, and all the Philistines; and wherever they went, they won deliverance and great might.
And at that same time he struck down Amalek and delivered Israel from the hands of their enemies.
And the sons of Saul were Jonathan, Ishvi, Melchizedek and Ishbaal. And the names of his two daughters are these: the elder was Merab (written Nerob), and the younger was Michal.
And the name of his wife was Achia, daughter of Ahimaaz; and the name of his commander-in-chief was Abner, son of Ner, servant of Saul.
And the name of his father was Kish; and Ner was the son of Iaben [?], son of Abiel.
And the struggle of war against the Philistines grew very fierce all the days of Saul, and he ordered every strong and valiant man to be in his service.
At that time Samuel came to Saul and said to him: "The Lord your God sent me to anoint you king over Israel, his people! Now listen to the command of the Lord.
For thus says the Lord Almighty: Behold, I will take vengeance on Amalek, because they did evil to my people when it was coming out of the land of Egypt.

And now arise, go, come upon them and destroy Amalek and everything that is theirs: man and woman, child and suckling, ox and sheep, camel and ass [?]. Destroy and slaughter them all, and leave nothing.

And Saul commanded that all the people be called together, and he gave his charge at Gilgal. When they were reviewed, about four hundred thousand men of Israel were found there, and three hundred thousand men of Judah.
And Saul went with the people and came to the cities of Amalek, and he lay hidden in the ravines of the torrent-bed.

And Saul said to the Kenite: "Go away from Amalek and do not come near it, because you did good to the sons of Israel when they came out of the land of Egypt, and I do not want evil to befall you." And when the Kenite had separated from Amalek,
Saul fell upon Amalek and slew Amalek from Havilah as far as Shur [?], which is opposite Egypt.
And he took Agag, the king of Amalek, alive. Saul did not do as the Lord had commanded him, but slaughtered only the worthless.

But the young-looking men and the very finest he carried off as captives, and he drove off the choicest of the flocks and all the good things of that land. Only the despised among them did he slaughter, and he brought King Agag along as a prisoner.
And as he was bringing King Agag along as a prisoner, the command of the Lord came upon Samuel, and he said to him:

"I regret that I set up Saul as king, because he has transgressed my command and has not done what I commanded him. Now go and say to Saul: 'The Lord has torn your kingdom away upon the earth!'" And that word grieved Samuel, and he lamented to God all night.

And Samuel rose early in the morning and went to meet Israel at dawn. And they told Samuel: "Saul has come to Carmel." And he set up his hand [i.e. a monument], turned his chariots around, and went down from there to Gilgal. And Samuel came to Saul and saw Saul, for he was offering a sacrifice to the Lord from the spoil that he had taken from the Amalekites.
And when Samuel came to Saul, Saul said to him: "Blessed of the Lord, behold, I have carried out every command of the Lord."
Samuel answered and said: "Then what is this sound of sheep that I hear with my ears?"
Saul answered and said: "Those are the very choicest, oxen and sheep, which this people spared to offer to the Lord; but the rest they destroyed."
Samuel answered Saul and said: "Now listen, and I will tell you the command of the Lord that the Lord spoke to me this night." And Saul said to him: "Speak."
Then Samuel said: "Were you not the least among the tribe of Benjamin, and the Lord anointed you king over all Israel?
And he sent you on a mission and said to you: 'Go and destroy, slaughter Amalek, which has sinned against me, completely.'
But you did not carry out the command of the Lord; instead you let your eyes loose on the spoil, and you did evil before the Lord."

And Saul said to Samuel: "Because I listened to the voice of this people. And I went on the mission on which you sent me, and I brought Agag, king of the Amalekites, alive as a prisoner, and I destroyed the people of the Amalekites.
And I drove the very choicest oxen and sheep to Gilgal to offer to the Lord God."

Samuel answered Saul and said: “The Lord does not want offerings as sacrifice, but the acknowledging of his command! For obedience is far better than sacrifices, and hearing the command of the Lord is better than the fat of rams.

For the ‘word of words’ [?] is sin, and vain anger is lawlessness, and luxury brings on sickness and pain. Now, because you have despised the command of the Lord, the Lord will despise you too, so that you will no longer reign over Israel.”
Then Saul said to Samuel: “I have sinned before the Lord, for I transgressed the command of the Lord and your word. I was afraid of the people and gave in to them.
Now forgive me this sin of mine, and come with me, and let us go and worship the Lord your God.”
Samuel answered Saul and said: “I will not go with you, for you have despised the command of the Lord, and now the Lord will despise you, so that you will no longer reign over Israel!”
Samuel turned around to go away from him, and Saul took hold of his garment to keep him there with him, and one edge of his garment tore off.
Then Samuel said to him: “So will the Lord tear away your kingship over the land and over the house of Israel this very day, and give it to your neighbour, who is better than you.
He will divide Israel in two, and he will not turn back, nor will the Holy One of Israel repent, for he is not like a man, that he should repent of that wrath.”
Saul said to Samuel: “I have sinned, but do not disgrace me any further before the elders of my people and before Israel. Come back with me, and let us worship the Lord your God.”
So Samuel went with Saul, and they worshipped the Lord.
Samuel said: “Bring Agag, king of Amalek, to me!” They brought Agag to him from Anathoth [?], and trembling took hold of him, and he said: “Is death really this bitter?”

Samuel said to him: “As your sword made women childless, so will your mother be made childless among women, among the sons of Asher [?]!” And Samuel struck King Agag and killed him before the Lord at Gilgal.
Samuel went away to Armathaim, and Saul went to his own house, there at the Hill.
Samuel did not see Saul again until the day of his death, because Samuel mourned for Saul. And the Lord also repented that he had made him king over Israel.

The Lord said to Samuel: “How long will you mourn for Saul? For I have also rejected him, so that he will no longer reign over Israel.” Then the Lord said to Samuel: “Fill that horn of yours with oil, and I will send you to Jesse in Bethlehem, for I have chosen a king for myself from among the sons of Jesse.”

Samuel answered the Lord and said: “How can I go? Saul might find out and kill me.” The Lord said to Samuel: “Take a heifer from the herd [?] with you, and say: ‘I have come to offer sacrifices to the Lord.’
Invite Jesse and his sons to the sacrifice, and I will show you what you are to do. Anoint for me the one I name to you.”
Samuel did everything the Lord had commanded him. He came to Bethlehem, and the elders of the city were astonished at his arrival, and they said to him: “Is your coming to us peaceful, seer?”

And he said: "It is in peace, for I have come to offer sacrifice to the Lord God. Now sanctify yourselves, and sit down [?] with me at this sacrifice today, at this hour!" And he sanctified Jesse and his sons, and called them to the sacrifice.
And they came before him, and when he saw Eliab he said: "Surely this is the Lord's anointed before the Lord?"

And the Lord said to Samuel: "Do not look at his appearance, nor at the height of his stature, for I have rejected him. For God does not see as a man sees: a man looks only at the face, but God knows the heart."
And Jesse called Abinadab and presented him before Samuel, and he said: "God has not chosen this one either!"
Then he presented Shammah to him, and Samuel said: "God has not chosen that one either!"
And Jesse presented all seven of his sons before Samuel. And Samuel said to Jesse: "The Lord has not chosen any of these."

Then Samuel said to Jesse: "Are these all your sons?" And he said: "There is still one more, the youngest, out with the flock of sheep." And Samuel said to Jesse: "Send quickly and bring him here, for we cannot sit down [?] until he comes here."

And Jesse sent, and they brought him before Samuel. And he was ruddy of face, cheerful, with beautiful eyes, and handsome in appearance. Then the Lord said to Samuel: "Arise quickly and anoint him, for I have chosen him!"
And Samuel took the horn of anointing oil and anointed him in the presence of his brothers. And the Spirit of the Lord came upon David from that day on for a long time. And Samuel went away to Ramah.
And the Spirit of the Lord departed from Saul, and an evil spirit entered him by the command of the Lord and tormented him.
Saul's servants answered and said to him: "See, an evil spirit from the Lord is choking you.

Now listen to the word of your servants, and let us seek for our lord a man who knows the art of the songs of the Lord on the lyre. And whenever the evil spirit from the Lord comes upon you, he will recite that song of the Lord on the lyre, and it will be good for you, and you will find relief."
Saul said to his servants: "Go and seek out for me a man who sings the song of the Lord well, and bring him to me."

One of his servants answered and said: "I have seen among the sons of Jesse in Bethlehem one who sings the art of the Lord well and with skill; he is a wise man, mighty in strength, brave, prudent in speech, and handsome in appearance, and the Lord is with him."
And Saul sent messengers to Jesse and said: "Send me David your son, who is with the flock of sheep."
And Jesse loaded onto a donkey [?] one measure [?] of bread, one skin of wine, and one young goat, and sent them by David his son.
And David came in and stood before him, and Saul loved him greatly. And David became his armour-bearer.
And Saul sent a man to Jesse and said: "Let David stand before me always, for he has found favour in my sight."

And whenever the evil spirit from the Lord came upon Saul, David would take the lyre and sing before him, and he would bring Saul relief, and it would please him, and the evil spirit would depart from him.
At that time the Philistines gathered, came and set up camp in battle formation between Socoh and Azekah, in Ephermin.
Saul and the people of Israel gathered, came and set up camp in the Valley of the Oak, facing them. They drew up in battle lines against each other on either side.
The Philistines stood on the mountain on the far side, the Israelites stood on the mountain on the near side, and the valley lay between them.
Then a man came out from the Philistine people. He was a mighty man from Gath. His name was Goliath, and his height was four cubits and a span.
He was armed like a nobleman, with a coat of chain mail and a helmet. His armour weighed five thousand shekels of iron and bronze.
He held a bronze shield in his hands.
The shaft of his spear was like a weaver's beam. The head of his spear weighed six hundred, and an armour-bearer went in front of him.

He came and stood ready before the Israelites and said: "Why have you all lined up together to fight us? Look, I am one of the Philistines, and you are Saul's Hebrews. Now choose one man to come out and fight me.
If he beats me and kills me, we will be your subjects. But if I beat him and kill him, you will be our subjects."
The Philistine spoke again: "Look, this very day I defy the battle lines of Israel. Let one man among you come out, and let the two of us go out bravely to meet each other alone."
When Saul and the Israelites heard these words of the Philistine, they were struck with terror, because they were very afraid.
David was the son of an Ephrathite man from the city of Bethlehem, of the tribe of Judah. The man's name was Jesse. He had eight sons, and he was old.
His three younger sons had gone with Saul to the battle. These are the names of Jesse's three sons: Eliab, Aminadab and Shammah.
David was the youngest of them, and these three had gone to Saul.
But David went to Bethlehem to tend his father's sheep.
The Philistine would get up early and stand from morning until evening, like a pillar, in front of the Israelites.
At that time Jesse said to his son David: "Take with you a measure of roasted grain and ten loaves of bread. Hurry to the camp and give them to your brothers.
Give these ten almonds to the commander. Find out how your brothers are doing, and come back and tell me how they are."
Saul and all their people were standing in battle formation under the oak in the valley of battle, facing the Philistines.
David got up early at dawn and left the sheep in the care of the shepherds. He did what Jesse had told him and came to the battlefield. The people of Israel shouted and raised a war cry.
They went out, and each man stood in his place, ready for battle. In the same way the Philistines came and stood facing the Israelites.
David took his baggage and left it with the keeper of the baggage. He went with the people into the battle and asked how his brothers were.
While he was still saying this, the man named Goliath, the Philistine from Gath, came out. David and all the people of Israel heard him, because he was speaking arrogant words with insolence.
When they saw the man, they were very afraid and turned and ran from him.

And a certain Israelite man said to his companion: "I know how this man has come out to reproach Israel. But as for whoever kills him, I know that the king will make him rich, give him his daughter as a wife, and make his father's house free in Israel."

When David heard this, he said to the men who were around him: "What good will be done for the man who kills him, this man who reproaches the people of Israel? And who is that uncircumcised man who has come out to reproach the people of the living Lord God?"
Someone from the battle line there answered him with the same words and said: "It will be given, as promised, to whoever kills him."

When Eliab, his brother, heard these words that David was speaking to the men, he grew very angry with David and said: "Why have you come down here? And to whom have you left those poor sheep? I know your pride and your wickedness, for in your insolence you have come here to see the struggle of the battle."
David answered and said to him: "And now what have I done to you? I only said one word. Or did I take something from you?"
And David went to another place and said the same thing, and some of the people there answered him just as before.
And David's words were reported to Saul, and they brought David and set him before Saul.
David began to speak before Saul and said: "Do not be dismayed, my lord king, for I, your servant, will go out and fight with that foreigner."
Saul answered David and said: "You are a boy, and he is a mighty man and has been a warrior since his youth. You cannot stand against him."
David began to speak to Saul and said to him: "When I was tending my father's flocks in the wilderness, a lion or a bear would come and carry off a ram or a goat,
and I would chase after it and take it out of its mouth. And if it attacked me, I would wrench its limbs, crush it, and kill it.
And now let that uncircumcised foreigner be counted as one of the evil beasts. Why should I not go and kill him and take away the reproach from Israel today? For who is this uncircumcised man?"

Then David said: "The Lord himself, who saved me from the mouth of the lion and from the paws of the bear, will save me from the hands of that uncircumcised man and of the foreigners!" Saul answered David and said: "Go, go out, and may the Lord be with you."
And Saul put a coat of mail on David, and over the mail a cuirass [?], and he set a bronze helmet on his head.

And he fastened his own sword around his waist. But when David went to walk, he began to totter [?] and stumble, because he was not used to it. David answered Saul and said: "I cannot go out in this, for I have never tried it and I am not used to it." David stopped where he stood and took the armor off.
And he took his staff, chose five smooth stones from the riverbed, and put them in his shepherd's bag. He took his sling in his hands and went out against that foreign giant.
And from the other side the foreigner moved forward and came toward David. As he came near him, he stopped where he stood, and a shield-bearer went in front of him, shielding him.
And when the foreigner Goliath saw David, a handsome young man, ruddy and good-looking, he despised him.
He cried out and said, "Am I a dog, that you come against me with a staff and stones?" And the Philistine cursed David by his idols.
And he said, "Come [?], come out to me, and I will give your flesh as food to the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth."

David answered and said to him, "[?], you come against me there with a coat of mail, a spear and a shield. But I come against you in the name of the Lord God, who does as he wills [?], and for the sake of this people Israel, whom you have taunted today in your arrogance.

For today the Lord God has delivered you into my hands and has slain you on this spot [?]. With your own sword I will cut off your head, and I will give your flesh and the flesh of that Philistine people as food to the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth. And all the nations of the earth will know that there is a God of Israel.
And all the people will know that the Lord does not save by sword, nor by spear and mail, but victory in battle comes from the Lord. And the Lord has given you over into my hands."
The Philistine rose and came against him, and as he drew near to David, he hurried toward him.

And David put his hand into the bag, snatched out a stone, put it in his sling, slung it, and struck the Philistine on the forehead. He broke his forehead, helmet and all, and drove it into his brain, and he fell face down on the ground.
And David prevailed over the Philistines that day, for he killed the Philistine with a sling and a stone, and he had no sword, no weapon and no spear.
David ran and came to the Philistine. He set his knee on his neck, drew out his sword, and cut off his head, helmet and all. When the Philistines saw that their mighty man had been killed, they fled.

The [?] of Israel and Judah raised a shout and rushed upon them, and they destroyed the fleeing Philistines and laid them down as corpses one after another as far as Gath and as far as the gates of Ashkelon. And many wounded Philistines fell.
And the people of Ashkelon came out and fell upon the spoil and plunder of their camp, and they stripped their corpses.
And David took the Philistine's head to Jerusalem, and he took his coat of mail and his armour for his own dwelling.

And when Saul saw David going out against the Philistine, he said to Abner, the commander of his army, "Whose son is that youth?" Abner answered and said, "As your soul lives, my lord the king, I do not know."
And when David came back from his feat of valour, having killed the Philistine, Abner took him by the hand and brought him before Saul, and the champion's head was in David's hands.
Saul answered and said to him, "Whose son are you, young man?" David answered and said, "I am the son of your servant Jesse the Bethlehemite."
And when David had told the king this, Jonathan, the king's son, came to love him with a great love, as his own self.
And from that day Saul kept David with him and no longer let him go back to his father's house.
And Jonathan made a covenant with David, because he loved him as his own self.
And Jonathan took off his robe and gave it to David, along with his coat of mail, his sword, his bow and quiver, and all his armour, down to his belt.

And Saul set him over the men who fought for his people. David went out and came in with understanding before the Lord and as a commander before him. He was pleasing in Saul's sight in all his deeds, and in the sight of all Saul's people.
