And it happened, when they were coming back from the slaughter of the foreigners, that the dancing women [?] came out from all the cities of Israel to meet David and Saul. They sang before them with drums [?], pipes and lyres, [?] and cymbals.
They opened their mouths and went out to meet them, playing and praising and saying: “Saul has slain thousands, but David has struck down tens of thousands.”

Saul grew angry, because these words displeased him, and he said: “How is it that they have given David the slaughter of tens of thousands, and me only of thousands? What else does he lack now, except only these royal diadems of mine?”
And from that time on he looked on David with suspicion, to the very end.

And it happened on the next day that an evil spirit from the Lord came upon Saul, and he was tormented in his own house. David was playing the music of blessing, as he was always accustomed to do, and Saul had a spear in his hands.
He meant to strike David and pin him to the wall with that lance. And David turned aside from before the sword twice.
And Saul was afraid of David, because the Lord had left him and was with David.
So Saul removed David from his presence and appointed him commander over his people. And David went in and came out before Saul.
And David had understanding in all his ways, for the Lord Almighty was with him.
And Saul saw David's wisdom and was greatly afraid.
And all Israel loved David, because he went in and out of Saul's household.

Saul began to speak to David and said: “Behold, I have given you my daughter Merab as your wife. Be a son and a strength to me, and fight against the enemies of the Lord.” For Saul thought this: “Why should I myself [?] lay my hand on him? Rather, let the hand of the foreigners be upon him.”
David answered Saul and said: “Who am I, or what am I, or what is my father's family in Israel, that I should be found worthy to be your son-in-law, O king?”
And after some time, when Merab, Saul's daughter, had been betrothed to David as his wife, the girl did not want to become David's wife, for she had been betrothed as wife to Eli [?] the Meholathite.
And Michal, Saul's daughter, loved David. When Saul learned of this, it seemed very good in his eyes.

And Saul said: “I will give her to him as his wife, so that she may be a snare to him and the hand of the foreigners may be upon him.” And Saul said to David: “From this day on you shall be called my son-in-law among the people.”

And Saul commanded his servants and said to them: “Go and say to David in secret: ‘Behold, the king wishes you to become his son-in-law, and all his servants love you. Now agree to become the king's son-in-law.’”

So the servants came and spoke to David as the king had commanded them. David answered and said: “Let it not seem a small thing in your eyes to become the king's son-in-law, for I am a poor man, and I am not of a great or honoured family.”
And they told Saul all of David's words.

And Saul said to his servants: "Say this to David: 'There is no question of a request here. It is not that anything seems hard to you, or that he needs anything more. There is only this as your gift to him: the bodies of a hundred men, all at once, from among the king's enemies.'" For Saul had planned this: "How can I throw David into the hands of the Philistines?"
And they went and told David everything Saul had said. It pleased David to become the king's son-in-law and to bring the gift that Saul was asking of him.

And before even a little time had passed, David went with some men and struck down the Philistines, about a hundred men. He brought what had been taken from the hundred men, as the king had asked of him. From then on he was the king's son-in-law, and Saul gave him his daughter Michal as his wife.
When Saul learned that the Lord God was with David, and that his daughter Michal and all Israel loved him,
Saul feared David even more, and Saul was David's enemy all the days of his life.
The princes of the Philistines came out at untimely moments, and David was valued and honoured more than all of Saul's servants.
After this Saul made plans with his son Jonathan and with all his servants to kill David. But Jonathan, Saul's son, loved David very much.
And at once he revealed it to David and said to him: "My father is watching for a chance to kill you. Now guard yourself. Tomorrow at dawn, go and hide in a certain place.
And I will go in to my father myself and find out from him what is in his heart, and I will let you know."

And Jonathan went in to his father Saul to ask for good on David's behalf. He said to him: "King, do no evil to David, for he has not sinned against you. Instead, all his deeds toward you have been good.

For he put his life at your service and gave himself into the hands of the enemies. He killed that Philistine in front of you, and by his hand a great salvation was brought about for Israel, and all Israel saw it and rejoiced. So now why do you sin, shedding the blood of a righteous man and putting him to death without cause?"
When Saul heard these words of Jonathan, he swore and said: "As my Lord lives, David shall not die."
Then Jonathan called David and told him what Saul had said about David. Jonathan brought David before Saul, and David was with him as he had been yesterday and the day before.
Then the struggle of war against the Philistines grew again. David grew stronger and stronger; he slaughtered those Philistines and put the rest of them to flight.
And the evil spirit from the Lord came upon Saul. He was sitting in his house with a spear in his hands, and David was playing before him gently [?].

And Saul was looking for a chance to run David through. He hurled the spear at David but did not hit him, for David turned aside, and the spear stuck in the wall. And David came out and went away from him.

That same night Saul sent chosen men to David's house to watch him in his house and to kill him at dawn. And Michal, his wife, told David about it and said to him: "If you do not get away this night and save your life, tomorrow you are a dead man!"
And Michal let him down through the window. He fled and escaped death at Saul's hands.
And Michal made something on his bed like a tomb, in the shape of a person's body. She laid one clump of hair [?] on it and covered it with a garment.
Then Saul sent men again to seize David. And Michal said to the messengers, "He is sick, lying on the bed, and struggling for breath." And they told this to Saul.
And Saul again sent messengers for David and said, "Bring him to me here on that same bed, so that I may kill him."
And the messengers came and saw the bed, made up to look like a tomb, and they went and told Saul about this.

And Saul said to Michal, "Why have you deceived me, and sent my enemy away so that he escaped from me?" Michal answered Saul and said, "He told me this: 'If you do not send me away, I will kill you.'"
David fled and escaped, and came to Samuel at Armathaim, and told him everything that Saul had done to him. And David and Samuel went to Naioth in Ramah and stayed there.
And they told Saul, saying, "Look, David is at Naioth in Ramah."
And Saul sent messengers to seize David. When they arrived, they saw a company of prophets prophesying, with Samuel among them. And the Spirit of God came upon Saul's men, and they too prophesied.
Saul heard this and sent other messengers, and they too prophesied. And Saul sent other messengers yet again, and they too prophesied.

And Saul became furious with great anger, and he rose and went to Armathaim himself. He came as far as that salty place, Sephina [?], and Saul asked, "Where are Samuel and David?" They answered him, "Look, at Naioth in Ramah."
And Saul went to Naioth in Ramah, and the Spirit of God came upon him, and he too prophesied.
And he stripped off his clothes before Samuel and prophesied, and he lay fallen naked all night. That is why people say as a proverb, "Is Saul too now among the prophets?"
And David came away from Naioth in Ramah and met Jonathan, and said to him, "What sin have I committed, or what evil have I done against your father, that he is seeking to kill me?"
Jonathan answered David and said, "Far from it! You will not die! There is no word of my father's, good or bad, that I would not know, and I would tell you all of it."

David answered Jonathan and said, "Your father knows that I have found favour with you, so he intends this: 'Do not let Jonathan know about this, so that he does not tell David.' But as the Lord lives, and as your soul lives, my death truly has been prepared in your father's presence."
And Jonathan said to David, "Tell me what you want, and I will know [?] that too."
And David said to Jonathan, "Look, tomorrow is a feast, and I am due to eat at the king's table. But send me away, and I will go and hide out in the field.
If your father asks about me, tell him this: 'David left me and went to Bethlehem, his own town, because the feast of offering sacrifices is being held there with his whole family and tribe.'
If your father says, 'It is good,' then you will know that all is well for your servant. But if he answers you harshly, you will know that he intends nothing but evil for me.

But you, show mercy to me, your servant, for today you have brought me into a covenant before God. And if you find any sin in me, your servant, kill me yourself, and do not bring me before your father.
Jonathan answered and said: Far be it! If I learn that my father is truly enraged against you, I will come and tell you, and you must flee.
David said to Jonathan: And now, who will come and tell me if your father perhaps answers you harshly about me?
Jonathan answered David and said: Come, let us go out into the field. And they went out.

And Jonathan said to David: The Lord God knows: I will question my father about you when the time is right, twice and three times. If he says anything good about you, I will send a man to you and let you know.
If he says evil, may the Lord do so and so to Jonathan if I do not let you know everything early and send you away from me in peace.
And if I am still alive, show me the mercy of the Lord;
if I die, do not withhold your mercy from my house for all time to come, even when the Lord wipes out your enemies;
and if he wipes out me, Jonathan, too, together with the house of Saul, may the Lord require it at the hands of David's enemies.
And Jonathan swore to David once more, for he loved him greatly.
And Jonathan said to him: Tomorrow is the feast of the new month. And when he sees your seat,
you, come three times and look at the place where you were hidden, and sit on that stone.
And I will come and shoot three arrows toward a mark [?].

And I will send my servant boy and say to the boy: Bring me my arrows that I shot. And if I say this to the boy: Look, the arrows are on this side of you, find them — then know that there is peace for you and no evil word; as the Lord lives.
If I say this to the boy: Search further on, beyond you — arise and go, for the Lord has sent you away in peace.
And as for the word that you and I have spoken, the Lord is witness between me and you, and between my descendants and your descendants, for all time to come.
And David went and hid in the field that Jonathan had shown him. And the feast of the new month came, and the king came to the hall to eat bread.
And the king sat in his seat, and after him Jonathan sat, and Abner came and sat beside Saul, but David's place remained empty.
And Saul said nothing to him that day, for he thought: Perhaps something has happened to him and he is not clean.
And on the next day, the second day of the month, Saul looked and saw David's place empty, and said to Jonathan his son: Why did the son of Jesse not come in yesterday or today to eat bread?
Jonathan answered and said: He asked my leave to go to Bethlehem, his city.

For he said to me: Let me go, for my kinsmen are holding a sacrifice, and my brothers have sent a man for me to come. Now, if I have found favour before you, let me go and see my brothers. And so he is not here, and for that reason he did not come in to eat bread before you.

Saul grew very angry with Jonathan and said to him: "You son of a woman, you woman-hearted one, raised as a girl! Do I not know that you are loyal to the son of Jesse? It is to your own shame, and to the disgrace of your mother's exposed nakedness.
For as long as the son of Jesse is still alive on the earth, your kingship will not prosper! Now send quickly and have him seized and brought here, for he is a son of death."
Jonathan answered Saul: "Why should he die? What has he done wrong?"
Saul snatched up the spear to kill Jonathan. Then Jonathan knew that his father truly wanted David's death.
Jonathan rose from the table in fierce anger and went out, and he ate no bread. His heart was broken for David, because his father had resolved to kill David.
The next day Jonathan went out to the field for the meeting he had arranged with David, and a small boy was with him.
Jonathan said to the boy: "Go, bring me back my arrows that I shoot."
The boy ran quickly to the place of the arrows that Jonathan had shot.
Jonathan called to the boy and said: "Hurry, quickly, toward you [?]!" The boy gathered up the arrows and brought them to his master.
But the boy did not know what they had planned. Only Jonathan and David knew.
Jonathan loaded his bow and his arrows onto the boy and said to him: "Go quickly, hurry to the city!"
David rose from his hiding place and bowed down to Jonathan three times. They kissed each other's faces and wept a long time over their parting.

Jonathan said to David: "Now go, and go in peace. Remember how we swore to each other in the name of the Lord and said: 'The Lord is witness between you and me, and between my descendants and your descendants.'"
David rose and went away, and Jonathan went into his own city.
David came to Nob, to Ahimelech the priest. Ahimelech the priest was astonished that David had come, and said: "Why is this, my lord? Why do you come alone, with no one with you?"
David answered him: "The king gave me an order and said to me: 'Let no one know about the matter I am sending you on.' I sent my servants on to a certain place, called Faithful, to wait for me there.
If you have bread with you, even just five loaves, give it to me, and if you have anything else, give me that too."
The high priest answered him: "I have no ordinary bread here at hand, only the bread of the offering. Now if your young men are pure from women, take it and eat."
David answered him: "We are pure from women. Since we set out on this journey we have been pure. And even if this journey is doubtful, today we would still be pure because of this vessel of mine."
Ahimelech took the bread and gave him the bread that had been laid out before the Lord. There was no other ordinary bread there, only the bread that had been laid out before the Lord.
A certain man of Saul's servants was there, a man sick in spirit, detained before the Lord. His name was Doeg the Edomite, Saul's mule-keeper.
David said to Ahimelech: "See whether you have a javelin, a sword or a spear anywhere here with you. I did not bring my sword with me, because the king's order was urgent."

The high priest answered him and said: "Look, there is the sword of Goliath the foreigner, whom you killed in the valley of Elah. It lies there wrapped in a garment. If you will take it, take it, for I have no other blade here except that one." David answered and said: "Give it to me, for there is none better than it." And Abimelech took the sword and gave it to David.
And David got up in haste and fled from Saul, and he went to Achish, the king of the Gittites.

Then the servants of Achish said to him: "Is this not David, the king of the land? Is this not the one whom the women singing praises came out to meet, saying: 'Saul has slain thousands, but David has struck down tens of thousands'?"
When David heard these words, he was very much afraid of Achish.

So he twisted his face in front of them and pretended to be mad. He danced and wandered from door to door as far as the city gate. Then he began to go on all fours, rolling about and drooling, and he let the spittle run down into his beard.
And Achish said to his servants: "Where did you find this man who is sick in his mind, that you have brought him before me?
Are we short of such sick men? From now on he is not to come into my house."
And David left that place and escaped, and he came to the caves of Adullam. When his brothers and his father's whole household heard of it, they came to him there.
And all who were in distress gathered to him, and he became their commander. There were about four hundred men.
And he went to Mizpeh of the Moabites. And David said to the king of Moab: "Let my father and my mother stay with you until I know what God will do for me."
And he persuaded the king of the Moabites, and they stayed with him for as long as David was in that distress.
And the prophet Gad said to David: "Do not stay in this city, but go to the city of Judah!" And David left there and came and settled in the city of Sarik.
And Saul heard that David had been found, along with the men who were with him. Saul was sitting on the hill among the ploughed fields with a spear in his hand, and his servants stood before him.
Then Saul said to the people: "Listen, sons of Benjamin! Will the son of Jesse really give you villages and estates, or vineyards, or will he make you commanders and captains of thousands?

For all of you stand here, and not one man among you was found who told me when my son Jonathan was making a pact with the son of Jesse. Not one of you felt sorry for me and told me when my son stirred up my servant to be my enemy, as he is this very day."
Doeg the Edomite, Saul's mule-keeper, answered and said: "I saw the son of Jesse when he came to Nob, to Abimelech the priest, the son of Ahitub.
He inquired of the Lord for him, and he gave him provisions, and he gave him the sword of Goliath."
And Saul sent for the priest Abimelech, the son of Ahitub, and for all the men of his father's house, the priests who were in Nob. And they all came to Saul.
And Saul said to him: "I am speaking to you, Abimelech, son of Ahitub!"

"Why did you conspire against me with the son of Jesse, giving him provisions and the sword of Goliath and inquiring of the Lord for him, so that he would rise up against me as an enemy, as he has this very day?"

Ahimelech answered and said: "And who among your servants has been as faithful as David? He even became the king's son-in-law, and ruler and administrator of all the affairs of the kingdom, commander and lord over the whole royal house."

"And what power do I have today to inquire of the Lord for him? Far be it, O king! Do not lay evil upon your servant, nor upon my father's house, for I know nothing of this plot, no matter great or small."
King Saul said to him: "You shall surely die, Ahimelech, you and all your father's house!"

And Saul said to his servants who stood before him: "Take these priests of the Lord and kill them all, for their hand is with David. They knew that he fled and did not tell me." But they were not willing to kill the priests of the Lord.

And Saul said to Doeg the Edomite: "Go and kill the priests of the Lord with the sword!" And Doeg the Edomite went and killed the priests of the Lord with the sword. On that day he slew three hundred and [?] men who presented themselves for the service of the Lord.
And Nob, the city of the priests, he struck with the sword, from man to woman, child and nursing infant, ox and sheep. He slew them all.
But one son of Ahimelech son of Ahitub escaped from there. His name was Abiathar. He fled and came to David and stayed with him.
And he told him of the slaughter of the priests.

And David said to Abiathar: "I knew it that same day, when I saw Doeg the Edomite, that defiled one, Saul's muleteer, and I said: 'He will tell all this to Saul.' Now I am guilty of their blood and of all your father's house."
"Now stay with me and do not be afraid, for I will avenge you as I would avenge myself. You are safe; stay with me!"

And they came and told David: "Look, the Philistines have come up and are fighting against Keilah. They are raiding the country around it, carrying off the livestock, eating up the threshing floors and trampling the fields."

And David inquired of the Lord and said: "Do you command me to go and strike down these Philistines and deliver Keilah?" And the Lord answered David: "Go and strike down the Philistines and deliver Keilah!"
The people answered David and said: "We ourselves are [?] and afraid. How shall we go into the valley of the Philistines?"
Then David inquired of the Lord again, and the Lord said to David: "[?], come quickly, for I have given them into your hands."

And David went to Keilah with the men who were with him and fought with the Philistines. David prevailed, and they fled before them. He struck them with a great slaughter, divided the plunder among the people, and delivered the city of Keilah.
And it happened that when Abiathar son of Ahimelech fled and came to David, he had the ephod with him.
Then they told Saul: "Look, David has come to Keilah!" And he said: "Now I know that the Lord has delivered him into our hands, for he has entered a walled city, secured with gates and bars."
Saul told all the people to come with him, to go down and fight at Keilah in order to besiege David and the people who were with him.

And David became aware that Saul was coming against him, for Saul had not forgotten the evil that he had plotted against David. David said to Abiathar the priest: "Spread out that ephod before the Lord!"
And David said: "O Lord God of Israel, your servant has surely heard that Saul is coming against me to Keilah, to destroy this city because of me."
"Now, will Saul come down here and besiege this city? Tell me, your servant, O Lord." The Lord God said: "They will besiege it."
And David said: "Will the men of Keilah hand me and these people of mine over into the hands of Saul?" And the Lord said: "They will hand you over."

And David rose quickly and went away, together with the people who were with him, about four hundred men, and they went wherever they could go. And Saul was told: "David has escaped." And he left Keilah, and Saul stayed his foot where he was.

And David came and stayed in the wilderness of Meseram, in the strongholds of Rubai [?], on the Armurovani [?] mountain. And Saul sought David all the days of his life, but the Lord did not give him into his hands.
When David learned that Saul was seeking him, David was staying on the Armurovani [?] mountain of the Ziphites.
And Jonathan, Saul's son, rose and went to David and lifted up his hands to the Lord.
And he said: "Do not be afraid, David! For my father will not find you, and you will reign over Israel, and I will be next after you. And Saul my father also knows this, that it is so."
And they made a covenant and set a testimony before the Lord. And David stayed there at the New Places, and Jonathan went to his own house.
And the Ziphites came to Saul at the hill and said: "Look, David is hiding among us in Meseram, in the strongholds, at the New Places, on the hill of Hachilah, which is on the south side of Jeshimon.
And every desire of your heart has been fulfilled, O king, for he has been shut up into your hands."
Saul began to speak to the people and said: "Blessed are you by the Lord, for you have had compassion on me.
Now go and be ready, and look over that place, and tell me truly, lest perhaps he deceive you by his cunning.
But find out truly the place where he is hiding, and come and tell me, and we will go prepared and search for him wherever he is hiding, with this thousand of the people of Judah."
And the Ziphites went away from Saul, and David was staying on the south side of Jeshimon.

And Saul went with his people to look for David. And David's lookouts told him: "Look, Saul and his people are seeking you." When David heard this, he went down to the rock that was in the wilderness toward Masman [?], and Saul pursued David into the wilderness of Maon.

And Saul was going with his people along one side of the mountain, and David was hidden away in flight from Saul. And Saul and his people surrounded David and his people who were with him. And just as they were about to seize them,
suddenly a messenger came from Saul's country and said to him: "Come back quickly, for look, the Philistines have invaded our land."
And at once Saul turned back and gave up pursuing David, and went to meet the Philistines. For this reason that place is called "Rock of Separation".
And David went away and stayed in the strongholds of Engedi.
When Saul returned from pursuing the Philistines, they told him, "Look, David has come to the wilderness of Engedi."
So he took a thousand chosen men with him and went to look for David. David was camped in front of Adaem.
He came to the place of the shepherds, and there was a cave there. Saul went into it to rest, and David and his men were hiding there.

The men who were with David said to him, "This is the day on which God promised you that he would give your enemies into your hands. Now do whatever seems good to you!" And David quickly went up to Saul and cut off a corner of his garment.
Then David regretted it in his heart.
He said to his men, "The Lord forbid that I should lay my hand on God's anointed."
With these words David held his men back, and he did not allow anyone to kill Saul. Then Saul came out of the cave and went on his way.
After that David also came out. He called to him, "My lord the king!" Saul looked behind him, and David fell down and bowed to him with his face to the ground.
David said to the king, "Why do you listen to the words of your servants who tell you that David is watching for a chance to kill you?
Look, your own eyes have seen that today the Lord handed you over into my hands. But I did not kill you, because I said, 'I will not lay my hand on the Lord's anointed.' Instead I spared you.
Now, my lord, see: the corner of your garment is in my hands. I cut it off your cloak [?], and I did not kill you. So understand now that there is no wickedness in me.
May the Lord judge between you and me, and may the Lord give me justice against you, for my hand will do you no harm,
just as the ancients said in their proverb: 'From the hands of the lawless comes sin.' Look, my hands have not been defiled against you.
Now whom are you, the king of Israel, following and pursuing? Are you following and chasing a dead dog, or a single flea in the wilderness?
May the Lord judge between you and me, and may he give me justice against your hands!"
When David had finished saying these words, Saul said, "Is this your voice, my son David?" And Saul wept aloud.
He said, "You are far more righteous than I am, my son! You have repaid me with good, and I have repaid you with evil in return for good.
Today too you have treated me well, as you have told me: the Lord shut me up in your hands today, and you did not kill me.
Who is there who finds his enemy in a tight place and does not kill him, but lets him go on his way in peace? May the Lord reward you with good for what you have done for me today.
Now I know for certain that you will surely be king, and your rule will extend over all Israel.
So now come and swear to me by the Lord that you will not wipe out my descendants after me, and that you will not destroy the line of my house from my father's house."
David swore it to Saul. Then Saul went to his home, and David and the men with him went up to Masepha, the narrow place.
At that time Samuel died. All Israel gathered and mourned for him, and they buried him in his tomb at Armathaim. And David went down to the wilderness of Maon.
There was a man in Maon whose flocks were at Carmel. The man was very rich: he had three thousand sheep and a thousand goats, and he was shearing his sheep at Carmel.
The man's name was Nabal, and his wife's name was Abigail. His wife was good in understanding and beautiful in appearance, but her husband was harsh, wicked and foul in his ways, and [?] in his mind.
And David heard that Nabal was shearing his flocks at Carmel.
So David sent ten of his servants and said to them: "Go to Nabal and greet him in peace from us.
Say to him: Thus says David: Peace and life be with you, with your house, and with all that is yours.
Now we have heard that your shepherds are shearing your flock. They were with us on Mount Carmel, and we did them no harm all the days they were on Mount Carmel.

Ask those shepherds of yours too, and they will tell you. So now let these servants of mine find favour before you, for we have come at a good time and on a good day. Now give this son of yours whatever your hand finds."
David's servants went to Nabal and told him everything David had said.

Nabal was agitated. He turned his head away in arrogance and said to David's servants: "Who is David, or who is the son of Jesse? These days there are many of them, and each one has left his own master and run away from his masters.
Shall I take my bread and my wine and the meat I slaughtered for my shearers, and give it to men when I do not know where they come from or who they are?"
The servants went away empty-handed and told David everything Nabal had said.

David said to the men who were with him: "Come, each of you take up his sword!" Each of them took up his sword, and David also girded on his sword. About four hundred men went with David, and two hundred stayed behind to guard the baggage.

At once one of the young men went to Abigail, Nabal's wife, and told her everything Nabal had said to David's servants. He said to her: "I have learned that David sent messengers from the wilderness to your husband, and he treated them as nothing.
Those men were very good to us. They did us no harm, and they never called us to account for anything.
All the days we were with them on the mountain, they protected us day and night while we were tending this flock.
Now consider in your mind what you will do, for evil is about to come upon Nabal's house. He is a [?] man, and no one can speak to him."

Abigail was alarmed and rose quickly. She took two hundred loaves of bread, two skins of wine, five sheep ready-dressed, five measures of parched grain, one measure of raisins and two hundred cakes of figs, and loaded them on donkeys.
She sent them on ahead with her servants and said to them: "Go on ahead, and I will follow behind you." But she did not tell her husband.
As she rode on her donkey and was coming down the slope of the mountain, David and his men were coming up toward them, and they met on the road.
Then David began to speak and said: "It was for nothing that I guarded all of Nabal's flocks in the wilderness and let no one harm them. And now he has repaid me evil for good."
"May God do this to David, and more besides, if by morning I leave a single boy of Nabal's household who turns to the wall."
When Abigail saw David, she quickly got down from her [?] (her mount) and fell on her face before David and bowed down to him.
And she said: "Let this sin be on me, my lord! Now let your maidservant speak to you, and listen to your maidservant."

"And let my lord not do evil because of that vile man, for his character is like his name: 'Bal' is his name, and lawlessness and folly belong to him. But I, your maidservant, did not see your servants whom you sent there."

"And now, my lord, as the Lord lives and as your soul lives, the Lord has held you back from bringing innocent blood on yourself and has kept your hand from avenging you. Now may all the enemies of my lord, those who seek evil against my lord, become like Nabal."
"And now accept this gift of blessing that your maidservant has brought to my lord, and give it to these servants of yours who stand before you."
"And forgive your maidservant's sin. The Lord will make my lord a sure house, the Lord God will fight my lord's battles, and no evil will meet you anywhere."
"If anyone rises up and seeks your life, my lord's soul will be bound in the bond of life, and you will crush the head of your enemies with your sling."
"And the Lord will do for my lord the good that he promised you, and the Lord will establish you as ruler and leader over Israel."

"And let this defilement and stumbling-block not come upon you, my lord: shedding the innocent blood of the righteous. May the Lord keep my lord's hand from taking his own vengeance. And may the Lord bring my lord joy. Then remember your maidservant and do her good."
David answered Abigail and said: "Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel, who sent you here today to meet me."
"And blessed are you, and blessed is your good sense, and may you be blessed, for this very day you held me back from going to shed innocent blood with my own hand!"

"But as the Lord, the God of Israel, lives, who held back my hand from doing evil to you: if you had not come to meet me, by morning not one of Nabal's household would have been left who pisses against the wall."
David took everything that Abigail had brought him, and David said to her: "Go in peace to your house. Know that I have listened to you and shown you favour."

Abigail went back to Nabal's house. He had held a drinking feast and was revelling as if at a royal banquet, and Nabal's heart was cheerful and very [?]. That day Abigail told him nothing at all, neither great nor small.
When morning came and the wine had worn off, his wife told Nabal everything that had been said. At once Nabal's heart died within him, and he became like a stone.
After that, when about ten days had passed, the Lord struck Nabal dead.

When David heard of Nabal's death, he said: "Blessed be the Lord God, who has judged the cause of my insult at the hand of Nabal, and has kept his servant from doing evil, and has turned Nabal's wickedness back on his own head." And David sent to Abigail to bring her to himself as his wife.
When the messengers came to Abigail at Carmel, they said to her: "David has sent us to you to bring you to him as his wife."
When Abigail heard this, she bowed down to the ground and said to them: "I am fit to be a maidservant, and to wash the feet of the servants of my lord."
And Abigail rose quickly and mounted her [?] (karauli), and took five maidservants along with her. She made herself ready and went with David's messengers, and became David's wife.
Then David took Ahinoam the Israelite, and both of them became David's wives.
And Saul gave his daughter Michal, David's wife, to Palti son of Amon.
At that time the Ziphites came to Saul and said: "Look, David is hiding among us on the hill of Hachilah, which faces Jeshimon."
And Saul came to the [?] (armurovani) wilderness, and with him three thousand chosen men of Israel, to search for David in the wilderness of Ziph.
And he came and camped by the hill of Hachilah, which faces Jeshimon, near the road, while David was staying by the road of the wilderness. And when David heard that Saul had come to search for him,
David sent out scouts to see whether Saul had truly come seeking to kill him.
David went secretly and came to where Saul was. Saul was asleep, and so was Abner son of Ner, his commander. A lamp was burning in front of him, and all the people were lying around him.
David spoke up and said to Ahimelech the Hittite and to Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab's brother: "Who will go in with me to Saul's camp?" Abishai said to David: "I will go in with you."
So David and Abishai went into Saul's camp by night. Saul was asleep, and a lamp and a spear stood in front of him, and Abner and all the people were asleep around him.
Abishai said to David: "Today the Lord has shut your enemy up in your hands. Let me strike him and kill him with his own spear and pin him to the ground."
David answered Abishai: "Far be it from you to kill the Lord's anointed and be held guiltless."
And David said: "As my Lord lives, unless the Lord puts him to death, or he falls in battle,
I will not lay my hand on the Lord's anointed. But now take that spear and the water jar from beside his head, and let us go."
So he took the spear and the jar, and they left. No one knew of it, and no one woke up, for they were all overcome by sleep, because a heavy sleep had been laid on them by the Lord.
And David crossed the valley to a distance, facing them, and stood on the top of the mountain.
And David called out to Saul's people and said: "Abner, Abner! I am speaking to you. Will you not answer me?" Abner answered and said: "Who are you who are calling me?"
David answered and said: "Are you not Abner, a chosen man in Israel? Why did you not guard your lord the king? For a man went into that camp of yours to kill your lord the king."

"This thing you have done is not good at all. As my Lord lives, you guards of your lord the king deserve death! Now get up and look for the king's spear and his water jug, which were by his head [?]."
Saul recognized David's voice and said, "Is that your voice, my son David?" David said to him, "Here I am, your servant, O king!"
David went on: "Why are you pursuing your servant, O king? How have I sinned against you, or what fault has been found in me?"

"Now hear the words of your servant, my lord the king! If God has stirred you up to pursue me, let God's will be done. But if it comes from men, may they be cursed before the Lord. For today they have driven me out so that I may not be settled in my inheritance. They said, 'Let him go away and serve that foreign idol.'"
"So now, do not let my blood fall to the ground before the Lord. The king of Israel has come out to hunt for me as someone hunts for a single flea, or a single night-bird in the wilderness."
Saul said to David, "I have sinned, my son David! Come back now, my son David. I will do you no harm, since you are so afraid of me. All the wrong is mine."
David answered him, "Look, I have left the king's spear here on this field. Let one of your servants come over and take it."
"May the Lord repay each person with justice, according to his own righteousness. The Lord handed you over into my hands, and I did not kill you, because you are the Lord's anointed."
"Now, just as you are honored and graceful in my eyes, may my soul be found joyful before the Lord. May he be my protector, remember me, and rescue me from every trouble."
Saul said to David, "You are blessed, my son David! May the Lord show you his mercy and rescue you!" Then David went on his way, and Saul went back to his own place.

Then David thought it over and said, "I might yet fall into Saul's hands, and that would not go well for me. Now I will go to the land of the Philistines. Then if Saul searches for me throughout all the territory of Israel, I will have escaped."
So David set out with his six hundred men, and he went to Achish son of Achinam, king of Gath.
David settled in Gath with King Achish: David himself, his men, his whole household, and both of his wives, Ahinoam the Israelite and Abigail, the wife of Nabal of Carmel.
Saul was told, "David has fled to Gath, in the land of the Philistines." After that Saul did not search for David any more.

David said to Achish, "If your servant has found favor in your eyes, give me a place in one of the towns, and I will live there. Why should I, your servant, live in your royal city, the seat of your inheritance?"
That same day King Achish gave him Ziklag. This is why Ziklag has belonged to the king of the Jews to this day.
David stayed there in the country of the Philistines for four months.
David and the men who were with him went out and raided the nearby country of the Geshurites, Amalek, and all the land whose people lived in peace from Geshur as far as the land of Egypt.

And he would lay waste their land and would leave no man or woman alive, and they would carry off as plunder their sheep and their cattle [?] and herds and camels and donkeys and clothing, and they came to Achish.
And they said to Achish: "Against which side did we make our raid today?" And he said to David: "To the south of Judea and the south of Remon, toward the Kenizzites."

And David would slay man and woman alike, and would not leave anyone alive to bring word to Gath, for he said thus: "Lest they tell the Gittites that David is doing this." And this was David's practice all the days that he dwelt in the land of the Philistines.
And David was greatly trusted by Achish, and Achish said: "David has now become ashamed to go to his people Israel, so he will be my servant for all time."

And it happened in those days that the Philistines gathered to make war on the Israelites. And Achish said to David: "Know that today you are with me to make war on Israel, together with your people!"
And David said: "Here I am! Now you will know what your servant will do before you!" Achish said to David: "Stand firm in that, and I will make you a ruler and lord over my house all the days."
And Samuel died, and all Israel mourned him, and they buried him in Armathaim, his own city. And Saul had destroyed every diviner, sorcerer and medium from his realm in the land.
And the Philistines gathered and came and encamped at Shunem. At that time Saul also gathered the people, and all the people of Israel gathered and encamped at Gilboa.
When Saul saw the camp of the Philistines, he was greatly afraid and his heart was dismayed.
And he began to inquire of the Lord, and the Lord gave him no answer. And he inquired through visions and through prophets, and from nowhere did he receive understanding of any word.

Then Saul said to his servants: "Seek out for me a woman who is a medium, and I will go and inquire of her about the matter." And his servants said to him: "Behold, there is a woman who is a medium in Endor."

And Saul put on other clothing so that he could no longer be recognized as king, and he covered his head and took two servants with him; and he came to the woman by night and said to her: "Divine for me by your necromancy, and bring up before me the man whom I seek!"

The woman said: "You yourself know what Saul has done, for he has destroyed all the soothsayers and diviners and mediums and those who speak from the earth. Now why are you hunting my life, to have me put to death?"
Saul swore to her by God and said to her: "As my Lord lives, no harm will come to you over this matter."
And the woman said: "Whom shall I bring up for you?" Saul said to her: "Bring up Samuel for me!"
In her [?] the woman first saw Saul, and the woman cried out and said to Saul: "Why have you deceived me and burned me as with fire? For you yourself are Saul."
King Saul answered the woman and said: "I told you already, do not be afraid, but tell me what you see!" And the woman said to Saul: "I see many idols coming up out of the earth."

And Saul said: "And what did you perceive?" The woman said: "I see a tall man coming up out of the earth, and he is wrapped in a double garment." And Saul understood that it was Samuel, and he bowed down to the ground and paid him homage.

Samuel answered and said to Saul: "Why have you troubled me and brought me up to you?" Saul answered and said: "I am in great distress, and the Philistines are fighting against me. God has cast me out of his hands and has not listened to me. I inquired by visions, by prophets and by signs, and still he did not listen to me. That is why I have called you up, so that you may tell me what I should do."
And Samuel said: "Why do you need to ask me, since the Lord has let you go from his hands and is with your neighbour?
He has done to you just as he told you through me: the Lord God will tear your kingdom apart and give it to your neighbour David!
For you did not listen to the command of the Lord, and you did not carry out your wrath in full against Amalek. That is why the Lord has done this to you.

And the Lord will give Israel, together with you, into the hands of the Philistines. Tomorrow, before this hour, you and your sons will lie fallen by the edge of the sword, and the people of Israel will be destroyed by the sword."
At once Saul fell face down on the ground, because terror took hold of him at Samuel's words. There was no strength left in him, for he had eaten nothing that day and drunk nothing.
And the woman
saw Saul, that he was in great distress, and said to him: "Look, your maidservant listened to your voice. I took my life in my hands and heeded your words!
Now you too listen to your maidservant: I will set bread before you, and you should eat, for you are travelling and you are weak."
But he refused. His servants and the woman urged him, and he would not listen to them. Only then did he get up and sit on the couch.
The woman slaughtered a suckling calf and made unleavened bread, warm.
She set it before them, and they ate it and went on their way all that night.
The Philistines gathered, came and camped at Aphek, and Israel camped at Endor, which is toward Jezreel.
The lords of the Philistines came on by thousands and by tens of thousands, and David and his band came along with Achish.

Then the lords of the Philistines said: "Who are these men marching beside this troop of ours?" Achish answered and said to them: "Is this not David himself, the servant of Saul, king of Israel? He has been with me for two years now, and I have not found a single act of deceit in him."

When the Philistines heard this, it displeased them greatly, and they said: "Send him back. Let him go to his place, where you have stationed him, and let him not come with us into this battle, so that he does not become a betrayer of this people of ours and bring great evil on us! For now he will reconcile himself to this lord of his with the heads of these men who are with us.
Or is this not that David whom the singers of praise came out to meet, saying: 'Saul has struck down thousands, and David tens of thousands'?"

Achish called David and said: "As the Lord lives, you have been upright and good in my sight, in peace and in battle. I have found no wicked deed in you toward me, and to these lords too you seem good [?].
But now go back in peace, so that these Philistines may not be displeased [?] with you."
David answered and said: "How have I sinned against you, or what evil have you found in me since I came before you, that you do not let me go with you to destroy the enemies of my lord the king?"
Achish answered David and said to him: "I know myself that you are pleasing to me, but these princes of the Philistines say this: 'David must not come with us into this contest of battle!'"

"So now rise at dawn and go to the place where I stationed you with your people. Do not take an evil word to heart, for in my eyes you are pleasing to me in every respect, like a messenger of God. Now rise early and go, and let the dawn find you on the road."
And David went away with his people, as King Achish had commanded him.
When David came into Ziklag on the third day, Amalek had already come to Ziklag.
They had taken the women and children captive, along with the livestock, and had burned the city with fire. However, they had killed no one. They had carried them off and gone on their way.
When David saw that their city had been burned and that their wives and children had been carried away,
David and the men who were with him lifted up their voices and wept greatly, until their strength gave out and they could weep no more.
Both of his wives had also been taken captive: Ahinoam the Israelite and Abigail of Carmel, the wife of Nabal.
David was in great distress, because the people plotted to stone David, for the people were enraged over their wives. But David was strengthened by the Lord.
And he said to Abiathar the priest, son of Ahimelech: "Bring out the ephod,
and ask the Lord whether I will somehow overtake that people." The Lord said: "Pursue them, for you will overtake them and recover the plunder!"
So David set out in pursuit with the six hundred men. When he came to the brook of Besor, he left two hundred men there to guard the baggage.
And he continued the pursuit with the four hundred.
There in the field they found an Egyptian man. They seized him and brought him to David. They gave him bread and water, and he ate and drank.
They also gave him a cake of figs and raisins, and his spirit returned to him, for he had eaten no bread for three days and three nights.

Then David questioned him and said: "Who are you, and where are you going?" He said: "I am the slave of an Amalekite man. My master abandoned me because I was overcome [?] by hunger, for this is the third day.
We went toward the south of Judea and Caleb and to Ziklag, and we burned Ziklag with fire."

David said to him: "And now, will you somehow lead me to their camp?" He said to David: "Swear to me by the Lord your God that you will not kill me and will not hand me over to my master, and I will lead you to their camp."

David swore by the Lord, and the man led him to their camp. David saw that they were spread out over the whole land, eating, drinking and rejoicing over the great plunder they had taken from the land of the Philistines and from Judea.
David came and fell upon them. He slaughtered them from dawn until evening, and on the next day he cut them down too. None of them escaped except four hundred young men, who mounted horses and fled.
David recovered the plunder and his two wives,
and he recovered all the plunder, great and small.
He recovered the flocks and their herds. They drove them ahead of David and went on. From then on it was called "David's plunder."
David came to the two hundred men who had been left to guard the baggage, and they came out to meet David and the people. David greeted them and asked after their peace and well-being.

Then the wicked and unworthy men who had been in the battle with David said: "The men who stayed here shall not receive a share. Let them take their wives and their children, and let them be cut off from us and from the rest of the spoil."
David answered and said to them: "It is not so. Rather, let us do this: since the Lord God has given our enemies into our hands, that word cannot be carried out,
but let all receive equally, the one who guards the baggage and the one who takes the spoil."
And they did so, and from then on it was set down as a law, according to the command and judgment of the Lord, in Israel to this present day.

And David came to Ziklag. He sent messengers and sent a share of all that spoil to the elders of Judah and to all its surrounding region, and said: "Let this be your share of this spoil from the enemies of the Lord": to
those who were in Bethor, those who were in Ramath of the south, those who were in Jattir,
those who were in Ariskhen [?], those who were in Siphmoth [?], those who were in Nooom [?],
those who were in Carmel, those who were in the cities of Israel, those who were in the cities of the Kenizzites,
those who were in Beersheba, those who were in the Negeb,
and in Hebron, and in all the cities to which David and the men who were with him had gone.
And the Philistines fought against the Israelites. Israel was given over to defeat. Every fighting man of Israel fled before the Philistines, and the wounded fell on Mount Gilboa.
The Philistines pressed hard upon Saul and killed Jonathan, Aminadab and Malchishua, the sons of Saul.
The battle grew heavy against Saul. The archers found him and wounded him severely, for they struck him in the [?] and drove arrows [?] into him.

And Saul said to his armour-bearer: "Draw your sword and kill me! Otherwise the uncircumcised may come and kill me, and mock me with scorn as my soul departs." But the bow-and-quiver bearer did not want to lay his hand on Saul, for he was very afraid. So Saul drew his own sword and fell on it.
When his bow-and-quiver bearer saw that Saul was dead, he drew his own sword and fell on it, and he too died with him.
So Saul died, and his sons, and his bow-and-quiver bearer with him.

The men of Israel who were on the other side of the valley and those who were beyond the Jordan saw that the men of Israel were fleeing. They abandoned their cities and fled, and the Philistines came and settled in them.
On the next day the Philistines came back to strip the corpses, and they found Saul and his three sons on Mount Gilboa.
They cut off his head and carried off his armour, and they sent messengers with the good news to their idols, to their people and to all their land.
They took their armour and laid it in the temple of their idols, and they hung his body on the walls of Beth-shan.
When the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead heard what had been done to Saul,
all the mighty men rose up and went and took the body of Saul and of Jonathan his son. They carried them up to Jabesh-gilead and burned their flesh with fire.
But they buried their bones in the field of Jabesh, and they fasted seven days.
